title: Senate Democrats accuse X of favoring Polymarket
content: Senate Democrats accused Elon Musk’s X of providing “preferential treatment” to the prediction market Polymarket on its timeline. In a letter sent Friday to X leadership, Democratic Senators Catherine Cortez Masto, Jacky Rosen, Adam Schiff, and Richard Blumenthal included screenshots alleging that the platform does not treat Polymarket equally.
summary: A group of Senate Democrats accused Elon Musk's X of giving the prediction market Polymarket preferential treatment on its timeline. The senators sent a letter to X leadership including screenshots that appear to show this bias.
author: The Hill

title: Talarico says he wants to work with Trump on bipartisan MAGA agenda
content: Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico stated his intention to collaborate with President Donald Trump on a bipartisan “Make America Great Again” agenda. During an interview, Talarico expressed his desire, as the next U.S. Senator from Texas, to work with Trump to fulfill promises associated with his political project.
summary: Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico stated he would want to work with President Trump on a bipartisan “Make America Great Again” agenda. He expressed his desire to fulfill some of the promises of Trump's political project during an interview.
author: The Hill

title: US to mediate Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi next week, Witkoff says
content: Special Envoy Steve Witkoff announced that the United States will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11. Witkoff stated on the social platform X that these talks aim to advance President Trump’s mission to end the war.
summary: US to mediate Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi next week, Witkoff says.
author: The Hill

title: Stevens explains rationale for endorsing Rogers over El-Sayed
content: Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) explained her decision to endorse former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan’s contested Senate race. Stevens cited campaign ads and other factors as part of her rationale. She stated that after concluding El-Sayed was not fit to serve in the United States Senate, she had to consider the alternative candidate.
summary: Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) shared her rationale for her recent decision to endorse former Rep.
author: The Hill

title: No Pro-Coal Candidates in Navajo Nation Presidential Election
content:
For the first time in decades, there is no pro‑coal candidate for Navajo Nation president.  

Coal has long been an important part of the economy, but voter sentiment is changing.
summary: For the first time in decades, the Navajo Nation presidential election has no pro-coal candidate. Voter sentiment is changing, as coal has been an important part of the economy.
author: NPR Politics

title: Red gold saffron harvested in Pampore, Jammu and Kashmir
content:
Kashmiri saffron is one of the world’s most expensive spices.

It is primarily cultivated in the Pampore region of Jammu and Kashmir in India. Often referred to as “red gold” because of its high value, saffron is prized for its rich aroma, distinctive flavour and quality.
summary: Kashmiri saffron is one of the world’s most expensive spices. It is primarily cultivated in the Pampore region of Jammu and Kashmir, India, and is referred to as ‘red gold’ because of its high value, prized for its rich aroma, distinctive flavour and quality.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Cervical cancer cases and deaths projected to rise by 20.2% and 39.3% by 2050
content: A modeling study published in Nature Medicine projects that global cervical cancer cases could increase by 20.2% and deaths by 39.3% by 2050. The analysis indicates that the disease burden will remain unevenly distributed, with the highest incidence and mortality rates concentrated in sub‑Saharan Africa.
summary: Cervical cancer cases and deaths projected to rise by 20.2% and 39.3% by 2050.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Plant compound may help overcome cancer drug resistance, study shows
content: A study by researchers at the Johns Hopkins Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center reports that a natural plant compound may help overcome a built‑in defense that allows many cancers to resist a class of drugs designed to restore normal gene activity. The compound could potentially counteract this resistance mechanism.
summary: A natural plant compound may help overcome a built-in defense that allows many cancers to resist a class of drugs designed to restore normal gene activity. The study was conducted by researchers at the Johns Hopkins Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center.
author: Medical Xpress

title: AI heart scan measurements better predict patient survival than clinician readings
content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) measurements of heart function derived from MRI scans show a stronger correlation with patient survival than measurements made by clinicians. The findings suggest that AI could serve as a useful first‑line method for assessing heart function.

The study was led by researchers at City St George's, University of London and University College London. It was published in The Lancet Digital Health.
summary: AI measurements of heart function from MRI scans are more strongly linked to patient survival than clinician measurements. The research, led by City St George's, University of London and University College London, was published in The Lancet Digital Health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New study finds nurses overlooked in One Health movement
content: A new paper argues that nurses are among the most vital components of the health care workforce, yet their contributions remain largely overlooked. The study examines nurses’ role within the expanding “One Health” movement, which seeks to link human, animal and environmental health.
summary: A new paper argues that nurses are one of the most important parts of the health care workforce. However, their contribution is overlooked in the growing "One Health" movement that connects human, animal and environmental health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors Benefit Adults 80+ with Chronic Kidney Disease
content: A study presented at Kidney Week, the American Society of Nephrology’s annual meeting in Denver from Oct. 21‑25, found that SGLT2 inhibitors provide significant benefits for adults aged 80 and older with chronic kidney disease.
summary: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors show significant benefits for adults aged 80 years and older with chronic kidney disease. The study was presented at Kidney Week, the annual meeting of the American Society of Nephrology, held from Oct. 21 to 25 in Denver.
author: Medical Xpress

title: 60% of Australians Eat Raw Fish, Food Safety Council Warns Ahead of Food Safety Week
content: Ahead of Australian Food Safety Week, Nov. 7 to 14, 2026, with the theme "Raw food know the risk," the Food Safety Information Council has released new research showing 60% of Aussies consume raw fish or seafood, and 17% do so at least once a week.
summary: The Food Safety Information Council released new research ahead of Australian Food Safety Week, Nov. 7 to 14, 2026, showing that 60% of Aussies consume raw fish or seafood. The study also found that 17% of Aussies eat raw fish or seafood at least once a week.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Toddler snacks pulled from Costco, Target, Walmart and other stores over choking danger
content:
Toddler snacks have been removed from Costco, Target, Walmart and other retailers after a federal health warning.  

Parents and caregivers are urged to stop serving Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels toddler bars immediately, as federal health officials warn the product could cause deadly choking.
summary: Parents and caregivers should stop serving Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels toddler bars right away because they could cause deadly choking, federal health officials warn.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Queen's University Belfast students find Neptune's elusive Trojan asteroids
content: An international team led by researchers at Queen's University Belfast has identified Neptune's elusive Trojan asteroids, resolving a long-standing astronomical mystery. While telescope observations beginning in 1906 revealed "Trojan" and "Greek" populations leading and trailing Jupiter, similar families were later found orbiting Saturn and Uranus. Despite these discoveries, astronomers had not previously confirmed the existence of such asteroids around Neptune.
summary: An international team led by researchers at Queen's University Belfast discovered Neptune's Trojan asteroids, a population that had eluded astronomers for decades. This finding resolves the long-standing mystery of Neptune's missing Trojan families, which were previously known only around Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus.
author: Phys.org

title: UK storm surges shaped by global climate patterns, Cambridge study finds
content: New research led by Cambridge University indicates that the specific location of storm surges along the U.K. coastline is determined by global climate patterns. These patterns extend across the Atlantic and Arctic regions, as well as areas even further afield, highlighting the far-flung connections between local coastal events and broader climate systems.
summary: New research led by Cambridge University shows that where a storm surge strikes along the UK coastline is decided by global climate patterns in the Atlantic, Arctic, and other regions. The study highlights that these patterns influence the surge location.
author: Phys.org

title: Analysis Links Square Chinese Characters to Linguistic, Technological, Cultural Factors
content: A new historical analysis published in the International Journal of Arts and Technology challenges prevailing views on the development of square Chinese characters. The study argues that these distinctive shapes emerged from interacting linguistic, technological, and cultural factors, rather than a single cause.
summary: A new historical analysis published in the International Journal of Arts and Technology challenges the received wisdom about why Chinese characters developed their distinctive square shapes. The study argues that the shape resulted from interacting linguistic, technological and cultural factors rather than a single cause.
author: Phys.org

title: PLOS Climate study finds tropical forests face shifting rainfall and extreme heat
content: A new study published in PLOS Climate shows that tropical regions previously considered safe from climate change are experiencing notable shifts in rainfall patterns and extreme temperature events. The paper, titled “Shifting climate in Caribbean tropical forests: Long‑term trends at La Selva (Costa Rica) and El Verde (Puerto Rico),” documents these significant changes in the Caribbean’s tropical forests.
summary: A new study finds that tropical areas often thought to be safe from climate change are experiencing significant changes in rainfall and extreme temperature events. The paper, titled "Shifting climate in Caribbean tropical forests: Long-term trends at La Selva (Costa Rica) and El Verde (Puerto Rico)," is published in PLOS Climate.
author: Phys.org

title: Ceres' Water Ice Masks Massive Surface Salt Deposits
content: The dwarf planet Ceres is described as one of the most overlooked objects in the solar system, largely because it is considered an "asteroid" despite sharing a dwarf planet designation with Pluto. Ceres resides in the main asteroid belt, where it stands as the largest object. Additionally, the dwarf planet accounts for between 25% and 30% of the total mass of the belt.
summary: Ceres, the largest object in the main asteroid belt, has water ice that can mask massive surface salt deposits. It accounts for between 25% and 30% of the belt's total mass.
author: Phys.org

title: Canadians Achieve Highest 2025 Federal Election Turnout Since 1993
content:
In the 2025 federal election, Canadians turned out to vote at the highest rate since 1993.  

Analysts typically explain variations in turnout by examining the national election campaign, noting how close the race was and what appeared to be at stake.
summary: In the 2025 federal election, Canadians voted at the highest rate since 1993. Explanations for turnout typically focus on the national campaign, such as race closeness and perceived stakes.
author: Phys.org

title: WorkOS reports security breach
content:
WorkOS has notified clients of a data security incident detected on October 30, 2026, at 16:39 UTC. The company identified anomalous traffic to an internal business system, with evidence suggesting the attack was driven by ARTEX, an AI-assisted autonomous penetration testing framework, from IP addresses in Hong Kong and China. The unauthorized actor accessed an internal API utilized by sales and marketing tools, which provided entry to Salesforce and Snowflake instances.

The compromised data includes business contact information, account and commercial details, aggregated product usage metrics, marketing contacts, and support tickets. Specific CRM information affected comprises names, email addresses, phone numbers, and company mailing addresses for WorkOS customers. WorkOS stated there is no evidence that application data or production services were accessed or impacted, indicating the incident was localized to CRM and customer support data. The company noted that the breach notification has not yet been posted on its website or Trust center.
summary: It's not on their website or Trust center yet, but we received the following breach notification from WorkOS: We are writing to notify you of a data security incident that we detected on October 30, 2026 and are continuing to investigate. We value your trust and want to keep you informed while our investigation continues.
author: Hacker News

title: User asks for contact to Cuyahoga Amateur Radio Club about removing radio gear
content:
A user posted on the Ask HN forum asking for help connecting with a Cleveland‑area ham radio club. The post explains that the user has already submitted a web form to the Cuyahoga Amateur Radio Club, but suspects the submission may have been “circular‑filed.” The user provided details about a large collection of radio equipment that must be removed from a home or it will be discarded; many items are brand‑new.

The user requests that anyone who knows someone at the club contact them and check the club’s web‑form intake. The post includes a link to the discussion thread on Ycombinator’s news site (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50346164) and notes that the item has received 92 points and 13 comments.
summary: I filled out the web form for the Cuyahoga Amateur Radio Club but it's probably been circular-filed... I gave some info about a large collection of radio gear that needs to be removed from a home or it will be put into a dumpster.
author: Hacker News

title: Show HN: Hacker Times, a New York Times‑inspired version of Hacker News
content: A new website called Hacker Times presents Hacker News content in a newspaper-style format inspired by The New York Times. The site updates once an hour, and the developer described the project as a fun way to browse the platform. The launch received 81 points and 30 comments on Hacker News.
summary: A new site called Hacker Times presents Hacker News content in a newspaper style, updating hourly. The post received 81 points and 30 comments.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors Program to supply up to 1,000 MW during emergencies
content:
OpenAI announced on Monday that it will pilot its “Grid Protectors Program” at a forthcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia. The company states the initiative will free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, a capacity sufficient to operate air conditioners in approximately 700,000 homes.

This announcement arrives amid increasing opposition to data centers across the United States. Local residents have frequently protested massive projects that begin development with little or no community input. In Utah, for instance, residents objected after Box Elder County commissioners approved a data center projected to consume more than double a specified amount of power.
summary: OpenAI announced a pilot of its Grid Protectors Program at a new data center in Effingham County, Georgia. The program aims to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in about 700,000 homes.
author: The Verge

title: Xbox’s former COO has ‘serious concerns’ about her abrupt departure
content:
Xbox’s former chief operating officer, Helen Chiang, left Microsoft less than two weeks ago after being promoted to the role in July. Chiang, who had spent 21 years with the company, received a surprisingly brief memo from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announcing her departure.

In a lengthy LinkedIn post titled “Clarity is Kindness,” a reference to Sharma’s Wall Street Journal profile, Chiang said she has “serious concerns” about how she was treated. She does not dispute that she was fired, but she does not disclose the reasons for her termination.
summary: Xbox's former chief operating officer, Helen Chiang, suddenly left Microsoft less than two weeks ago after being promoted into the role in July. I wrote in my Notepad newsletter last week that it seemed very weird for Chiang to suddenly depart Microsoft after 21 years with a surprisingly short memo from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.
author: The Verge

title: Large dogs age faster than small dogs due to epigenetic mechanism, study finds
content:
In October’s research roundup, a study published in Science explains why larger dogs tend to age faster than smaller ones. Arizona State University scientists found that the difference in lifespan is linked to “jumping genes,” or transposable elements, that influence DNA methylation patterns.  

Using data from 864 dogs in the Dog Aging Project, the researchers mapped genome‑wide DNA methylation—a chemical marker that regulates gene activity and changes over time. The study shows that these epigenetic changes, rather than fixed genetic sequences, correlate with the accelerated aging seen in larger breeds.  

Because dogs exhibit a clear inverse size‑lifespan relationship, they serve as a valuable model for biologists studying aging mechanisms across mammals.
summary: Arizona State University scientists found that large dogs age faster than small dogs because of epigenetic changes linked to jumping genes. They analyzed DNA methylation patterns in 864 dogs from the Dog Aging Project to map these aging differences.
author: Ars Technica

title: Smithsonian opens “At Home in Space” gallery, completing Air and Space Museum renovation
content: After seven years of work and nearly $1 billion, the Smithsonian has completed the renovation of the National Air and Space Museum's flagship building in Washington, DC. On October 30, the museum debuted its last-to-open spaceflight exhibition, returning "home" with a gallery devoted to establishing a spacefaring civilization. "Welcome to 'At Home in Space'!" said curator Jennifer Levasseur, who guided us through a virtual tour of the gallery. "This is the story of long-duration spaceflight in the last few decades. We generally call it 'reaching orbit.'" Read full article Comments
summary: The Smithsonian finished renovating the National Air and Space Museum’s flagship building in Washington, DC after seven years and nearly $1 billion of work. On October 30 the museum opened the “At Home in Space” gallery, the final spaceflight exhibition, with curator Jennifer Levasseur guiding a virtual tour.
author: Ars Technica

title: SpaceX aims to purchase Boost Mobile to challenge AT&T, T‑Mobile, Verizon
content:
SpaceX is reportedly interested in purchasing Boost Mobile, a move that would position the company against AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon. The potential acquisition is linked to SpaceX’s search for new applications of its Starlink satellite network.

A partnership with Boost Mobile could provide SpaceX with the terrestrial infrastructure needed to expand Starlink’s capabilities.
summary: SpaceX is reportedly seeking to buy Boost Mobile. The tie‑up could give SpaceX the terrestrial access it needs for Starlink and help it compete with AT&T, T‑Mobile and Verizon.
author: TechCrunch

title: Apple says iPhone Duo production rising but supply timeline uncertain
content: Apple said that production of the iPhone Duo is increasing, yet the company cannot predict when supply will match demand. It added that shipping delays are expected to continue into the following year, making it hard to forecast when the current constraints will ease.
summary: Apple says iPhone Duo production is ramping up. Apple cannot predict when supply will catch up with demand as shipping delays stretch into next year.
author: TechCrunch

title: Y Combinator Garry Tan says he spends up to $200K a year on AI tokens
content: Y Combinator partner Garry Tan admitted he uses AI agents so frequently that he spends up to $200,000 a year on tokens. Tan joked that this enthusiasm has led to “cyber psychosis” and occasional sleeplessness. In a recent episode of Walter Isaacson’s podcast The Builders, Tan discussed the cost of his passion.
summary: Garry Tan of Y Combinator said his AI agent usage can cost as much as $200,000 in tokens each year. He joked about suffering “cyber psychosis” and losing sleep while working with the agents on Walter Isaacson’s podcast The Builders.
author: TechCrunch

title: Kyiv startup makes 10‑ounce receiver letting Ukrainian troops view Russian drone video
content: A Kyiv startup has produced a pocket‑sized, 10‑ounce receiver that enables Ukrainian troops to view the video feeds transmitted by Russian drones. However, the report notes that Russian development of digital video and AI‑guided drones that emit no signals could limit the effectiveness of this capability.
summary: A Kyiv startup has created a pocket‑sized, 10‑ounce receiver that enables Ukrainian troops to watch video feeds from Russian drones. The benefit could be short‑lived as Russia moves toward digital video and AI‑guided drones that emit no signals.
author: TechCrunch

title: Trump Wraps Up Campaign in Iowa and Kansas as Democrats Target Congressional Control
content: US President Donald Trump concluded his campaign in Iowa and Kansas with a final push to rally support. Meanwhile, Democrats are working to regain control of Congress.
summary: US President Donald Trump concluded his campaign in Iowa and Kansas with a final push to rally support. Democrats are seeking to regain control of Congress.
author: Euronews

title: Trump says deal with Tehran could happen as Iran holds intensive indirect talks with US
content:
Trump has said a deal with Tehran “could happen” amid what he describes as “intensive” talks.  

Tehran announced on Monday that it is holding “intensive” indirect talks with Washington to avoid a fresh round of U.S. attacks on Iran ahead of this week’s U.S. mid‑term elections. Foreign‑ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Iran plans to reopen the blockaded Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. meets its demands.
summary: Trump said a deal with Tehran could happen as Iran and the United States engage in intensive indirect talks to avoid new US attacks ahead of the midterm elections. Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States meets its demands.
author: France 24

title: Éric Fassin says French student protests reflect an illiberal turn, not urban violence
content:
French student protests have been labeled “urban violence” by the Macron government, according to recent reporting. In a discussion hosted by Jennie Shin, sociologist Éric Fassin—professor at Université Paris 8—said elections are important but only the beginning of democracy. He described the protests as a growing challenge to socioeconomic policy and an “illiberal turn” in government, linking the treatment of working‑class, racialized youth to broader restrictions on dissent.

Fassin argued that racism and democratic participation are central to the unrest, contesting the tendency to assign blame solely to the left and situating the government’s response within a wider debate over the normalization of oppressive measures and the far right.
summary: Éric Fassin, a sociologist and professor at Université Paris 8, says the French student protest movement challenges socioeconomic policy and signals an “illiberal turn” in the Macron government. He links the treatment of working‑class, racialized youth to broader restrictions on dissent and argues that racism and democratic participation are central to understanding the unrest.
author: France 24

title: Fake nuclear warnings spoof Russia and Ukraine emergency alerts in overnight cyber attack
content: Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit in cyber attacks overnight, with fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes broadcast to users in both countries. The systems have since been brought back under control, though much remains unclear about the attacks, including who was responsible. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Dr Melanie Garson, Associate Professor in International Security at University College London. She says that these kind of attacks "are designed to undermine faith in the government's ability to provide trust".
summary: Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit by overnight cyber attacks that broadcast fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes. The systems were later restored, and Dr Melanie Garson said the attacks are designed to undermine faith in the government's ability to provide trust.
author: France 24

title: North Korea calls US claim of $6 billion Binance hack “absurd rhetoric”
content: North Korea on Tuesday dismissed US allegations that it was behind a $6 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance as "absurd rhetoric", accusing Washington of seeking to portray the country as a cybercriminal state and warning that US hostility could affect future diplomatic engagement.
summary: North Korea dismissed US allegations that it was behind a $6 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance, calling them “absurd rhetoric”. It accused Washington of seeking to portray the country as a cybercriminal state and warned that US hostility could affect future diplomatic engagement.
author: France 24

title: Russian strikes kill 26 in Ukrainian village after ceasefire ends
content: Russia’s strikes on a southern Ukrainian village on Monday killed at least 26 people, among them civilians gathering humanitarian aid, emergency workers and police officers. The attack occurred hours after a rare ceasefire ended, dashing hopes for progress toward peace.
summary: Russia's strikes on a southern Ukrainian village on Monday killed at least 26 people, including civilians collecting humanitarian aid, emergency workers and police officers. The attack occurred hours after a rare ceasefire ended.
author: France 24

title: European force to hold first Ukraine support exercise in Poland with 2,800 troops
content: European force will hold first Ukraine support exercise in Poland. About 2,800 troops from ten European nations will train in southeastern Poland from Nov 9 to 22. The drill, led by France and Britain, tests a multinational force intended to support Ukraine after a potential ceasefire, focusing on security assistance rather than offensive operations.
summary: Around 2,800 troops from 10 European countries will take part in a military exercise in southeastern Poland from November 9 to 22. The force, led by France and Britain, is designed to support Ukraine after a potential ceasefire and will not take an offensive role.
author: France 24

title: US reportedly strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Trump signals progress in talks
content: The United States reportedly struck Iran’s Qeshm Island on Monday, even as President Donald Trump signaled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight‑month‑old conflict. The attack was described as the latest in a series of limited strikes that Washington has secretly carried out in recent weeks.
summary: The United States reportedly struck Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday. President Donald Trump signaled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict, and the attack was the latest in a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out in recent weeks.
author: France 24

title: UK cyber agency says AI malware likely to target power stations, airports, hospitals by 2028
content:
The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) says AI‑powered malicious software is “highly likely” to be used in hacking attacks on the United Kingdom’s critical national infrastructure by 2028. It warns that AI could enable ransomware attacks against facilities such as power stations, airports and hospitals within that timeframe.

The NCSC notes that the UK’s definition of critical national infrastructure (CNI) encompasses a broad range of sectors, including energy, transport, defence, food, health and finance. The agency’s assessment highlights the growing threat posed by AI‑driven malware to these essential services.
summary: The National Cyber Security Centre says AI‑powered malicious software is “highly likely” to be used in hacking attacks on the UK’s power stations, airports and hospitals by 2028. The agency warned that AI could enable a ransomware attack against critical national infrastructure across sectors such as energy, transport, defence, food, health and finance.
author: Guardian World

title: US launches limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island as VP JD Vance expresses optimism
content:
Iranian state media reported hearing explosions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night, coinciding with the approach of the United States’ midterm elections. U.S. media outlets said the United States launched limited strikes on the island late that same day. The attacks were described as “defensive” and were not interpreted as a sign that full hostilities would resume.

The strikes occurred a few hours after U.S. Vice‑President JD Vance expressed optimism that diplomatic efforts to end the war were progressing in the right direction. Analysts noted that the timing of the strikes came on the eve of crucial midterm elections, in which Donald Trump’s Republican Party is expected to face voter backlash linked to the war’s impact on U.S. cost‑of‑living pressures.
summary: US media reported that the United States launched limited defensive strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island late on Monday, after Iranian state media heard explosions on the island. Hours later, US Vice‑President JD Vance said he was optimistic that diplomatic efforts to end the war were moving in the right direction.
author: Guardian World

title: Russian bombing of aid centre in Komyshuvakha kills at least 26
content:
Russian forces bombed an aid distribution centre and a neighbouring shelter in southern Ukraine, killing at least 26 people, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the country’s emergency services said.  

The strike hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the south‑eastern Zaporizhzhia region, where two members of a rescue crew and four police officers were among those killed. Five people, including two rescue workers, remain in hospital. Zelensky described the attack as “vile” and said it shows Russia does not want to de‑escalate.
summary: Russian forces bombed an aid distribution centre and a neighbouring shelter in the village of Komyshuvakha in south‑eastern Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 26 people. Among the dead were two rescue‑crew members and four police officers, and five people, including two rescue workers, were hospitalized.
author: Guardian World

title: Investigative reporter Kate McClymont testifies in Alan Jones indecent assault trial
content:
Investigative reporter Kate McClymont, the Sydney Morning Herald’s chief investigative journalist, testified in a Sydney court that the alleged victims of former radio broadcaster Alan Jones, whom she interviewed, received no benefit from her or the newspaper for telling their stories. McClymont’s 2023 articles prompted additional alleged victims to come forward, and she is providing evidence in the ongoing trial.

Jones has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching involving five men. The case remains lengthy as the former broadcaster faces the full slate of allegations.
summary: Kate McClymont, the Sydney Morning Herald’s chief investigative reporter, gave evidence in the trial and said the alleged victims she interviewed received no benefit from her or the media company for telling their stories. Former radio broadcaster Alan Jones has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching involving five men.
author: Guardian World

title: Court hears Beau Lamarre-Condon's voice notes on positive mindset after alleged murders
content: Recordings from police officer to man he’d met on dating app include one in which Lamarre-Condon states: ‘I’m in bed … not feeling the best’ Beau Lamarre-Condon said he was trying to “get back into a positive mindset” in voice notes he sent in the days after he allegedly killed two men in a Sydney terrace. The recordings were sent to a man he had met on a dating app and played to the jury in his double murder trial on Tuesday.
summary: Court hears Beau Lamarre-Condon's voice notes on positive mindset after alleged murders.
author: Guardian World

title: Reserve Bank of Australia raises cash rate to 4.85%, fifth hike this year
content:
The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised the official cash rate to 4.85%, the highest level since 2008. The increase moves the rate from 4.6% to 4.85% and marks the fifth rate hike the central bank has implemented this year.

The RBA said the move is intended to regain control of surging inflation, which rose to 4.3% in the year to September, amid a global oil shock linked to the war in the Middle East. The decision follows recent tough talk from senior central‑bank officials and is described as a further impact on mortgage holders.
summary: Reserve Bank of Australia raises cash rate to 4.85%, fifth hike this year.
author: Guardian World

title: Reserve Bank of Australia raises cash rate to 4.85%, fifth hike this year
content:
The Reserve Bank of Australia met today ahead of its cash‑rate decision and announced a rise in the official cash rate to 4.85%, up from 4.6%. This marks the fifth rate increase this year and pushes the cash rate to an 18‑year high.

The bank said the move is intended to regain control of surging inflation, which has risen to 4.3% in the year to September. Officials linked the inflation pressure to a global oil shock that follows the war in the Middle East. The increase is described as a further blow to mortgage holders, a consequence that was anticipated after recent comments from senior central‑bank officials.
summary: Reserve Bank of Australia raises cash rate to 4.85%, fifth hike this year.
author: Guardian World

title: Star Trek: The Original Voyages book to release Nov. 10, 2026
content:
Penguin Random House and Ten Speed Press will release "Star Trek: The Original Voyages: A Visual History" on November 10, 2026. The publication arrives following the celebration of the "Star Trek" diamond anniversary last month, which marked 60 years since the series first aired on NBC on September 8, 1966. The anniversary was commemorated with various events, including documentaries, special screenings, tributes, parade floats, and interviews.

Authored by Kyle Newman and Jeff Bond, the 416-page hardback serves as the first volume of a two-book series examining the complete history of the franchise. The book documents the classic characters and plotlines of the original television series, which the synopsis notes left an indelible mark on popular culture despite running for only three seasons and 79 episodes. According to the provided description, the series soon spawned an animated television series, a major motion picture franchise, and a way of life for dedicated fans.

The volume chronicles the story of the U.S.S. Enterprise and its crew, listing James T. Kirk (William Shatner), Spock (Leonard Nimoy), Leonard McCoy (DeForest Kelley), Montgomery Scott (James Doohan), Nyota Uhura (Nichelle Nichols), Pavel Chekov (Walter Koenig), and Hikaru Sulu (George Takei). It also covers the behind-the-scenes narrative of creator Gene Roddenberry and his collaborators. The text describes the series as a pioneering space fantasy that bolstered the space race and ignited the imaginations of sci-fi audiences by exploring strange new worlds and civilizations.

Readers of this collector’s edition will find archival photos, costumes, storyboards, props, filming models, and behind-the-scenes ephemera. The book extends its coverage beyond the original TV show to include the short-lived animated series and all six "Star Trek" feature films released up to 1991. Additionally, it details the franchise's broader cultural footprint, including licensed toys, comic books, convention memorabilia, media parodies, promotional roadshows, trading cards, and vintage magazine covers.

The release is priced at $60 and is described as an official visual history that documents how the iconic characters and storylines reshaped the science fiction genre. The synopsis states that few could have anticipated the enduring legacy created when the original series burst onto the screen in 1966. The book aims to provide an unprecedented exploration of the property, which continues to inspire artists, filmmakers, authors, and astronauts six decades later.
summary: Penguin Random House and Ten Speed Press are releasing "Star Trek: The Original Voyages: A Visual History" on November 10, 2026, to celebrate the franchise's 60th anniversary. The 416-page hardback, written by Kyle Newman and Jeff Bond, documents the original series, animated show, and six feature films through archival photos and behind-the-scenes materials.
author: Space.com

title: Juan Atkins, pioneer of Detroit techno sound, dies aged 64
content:
Juan Atkins, a pioneer of Detroit techno who performed as Model 500 and as part of the duo Cybotron, has died aged 64. His agency, Greensmith Artists, confirmed the news to Resident Advisor, noting his significant influence on dance music worldwide.

Atkins was found unresponsive in a hotel room in Mexico City prior to a scheduled performance there. He was subsequently taken to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
summary: Juan Atkins, a Detroit techno pioneer and former Model 500 and Cybotron member, died at age 64. He was found unresponsive in a hotel room in Mexico City before a performance and was pronounced dead after being taken to hospital, according to his agency Greensmith Artists.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Bad Brains: Pioneering Punk Band Known for Explosive Live Shows and Self‑Sabotage
content:
Bad Brains’ first sessions are being rereleased, and the band’s own interviews reveal how they once frightened club owners and were eventually kicked out of the UK.  The group, described as “young, black and fuelled by self‑help mantras,” still remains a point of contention among old‑school punks who debate who was first, who was fastest, and where to file the Faith/Void split LP in their collections.  Those who saw the band in its prime agree that Bad Brains were the best live act on the planet.

On YouTube, frontman HR—born Paul D Hudson—shows a blend of raw electricity and athleticism, bucking, contorting, and performing impeccably timed backflips while delivering rapid‑fire snarls and otherworldly croons.  The rest of the band surges around him, creating blisteringly fast punk that draws from the Damned, Dead Boys, P‑Funk, Stevie Wonder, and Chick Corea’s Return to Forever.

The band’s ideology combined 1930s self‑help teachings of Napoleon Hill with Rastafari, making them outliers in the 1970s punk scene.  Bad Brains helped reshape American punk into hardcore in the early 1980s and inspired artists ranging from Rage Against the Machine to the Beastie Boys, all while balancing celebrated live shows and a prolific record run with a relentless capacity for self‑sabotage.
summary: Bad Brains: Pioneering Punk Band Known for Explosive Live Shows and Self‑Sabotage.
author: Guardian Culture

title: I’m sick of smug celebrities on the podcast circuit. No wonder there’s a fuss when someone speaks the truth | Imogen West-Knights
content: It was so refreshing to hear Aaron Sorkin admit he was bad at parts of directing after his movie flop. If only others could be as frank By most accounts, Aaron Sorkin’s new film The Social Reckoning, a follow-up to his 2010 smash-hit The Social Network, is a flop. The film critic Mark Kermode’s response to seeing it was that Sorkin, who is widely regarded as one of the greatest living screenwriters, is “not a great director”. It seems that Sorkin agrees. Because Sorkin is very famous, he has had to do the rounds talking about the film in the media, which led to his appearance on the Hollywood Reporter’s Awards Chatter podcast earlier this week, in which he addressed these kinds of criticisms head on. “I’m very worried that the parts of directing that I’m not good at are those parts that you can’t learn,” he said. “In addition to having absorbed none of the science of filmmaking, I have – and this is a problem in a visual medium – I have no visual sensibility at all, it turns out.” Imogen West-Knights is a writer and journalist
summary: It was so refreshing to hear Aaron Sorkin admit he was bad at parts of directing after his movie flop. If only others could be as frank By most accounts, Aaron Sorkin’s new film The Social Reckoning, a follow-up to his 2010 smash-hit The Social Network, is a flop.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Baz Luhrmann’s 1996 Romeo + Juliet Turns Teens to Shakespeare
content:
Baz Luhrmann’s 1996 film Romeo + Juliet marks its 30th anniversary this week. The director’s maximalist, “heart over head” adaptation of Shakespeare’s romantic tragedy made the film’s leads—Leonardo DiCaprio and Claire Danes—stars and turned the movie into a trusted tool for English teachers working with students who are averse to the Bard. The film retains Elizabethan verse but immediately signals its departure from classicism, setting the story in a “fair Verona beach” that is relayed through a news‑anchor‑style TV set, followed by clips of civil strife.

Fresh off his breakout success with Strictly Ballroom (1992), Luhrmann re‑imagined the medieval family feud as a tropical gang war. He mapped the medieval narrative onto 1990s tabloid fixations, using grainy footage of street violence, magazine headlines about capos and criminals, and helicopter shots of car chases and riots that echoed the media circus surrounding the OJ Simpson chase two years earlier. The film’s portrayal of the two warring families as rival gangs, each with its own economic operations and marked territory, tapped into the era’s preoccupation with gangland as a source of transportive art—from movies to hip‑hop—and reflected contemporary concerns about intrinsic criminality.
summary: Baz Luhrmann’s 1996 film Romeo + Juliet turned Leonardo DiCaprio and Claire Danes into stars and became a popular tool for English teachers to introduce Shakespeare to reluctant students. The film reimagines Verona’s family feud as a tropical gang war, keeps the original verse, and celebrated its 30th anniversary this week.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Novelist warns of AI‑generated scam fan mail after replying to a fake reader
content:
A novelist reports that he receives a steady stream of fan mail every day, but the messages are not from genuine readers. The emails come from fabricated names such as Bella Monroe, Thalina Rose, and Tricia Claxton, and they are sent from cities including Barcelona, Frankfurt, Chicago, and Warsaw. The writer describes the tone of the messages as passionate and well‑informed, with some fans praising the “deadpan genius” of his novels and others admiring the “moral courage” of his nonfiction. The sender who signs off with “warm chaos” is an example of a more irreverent tone.

All of the emails are, however, entirely fake and are attempts to con the author out of money. The scammers promise to promote his work at city‑wide book clubs or within their reading communities if he transfers a few hundred dollars to cover costs. In the age of generative AI, the author notes that these scam emails have become highly personalized. They are sophisticated enough to bypass spam filters, forcing writers to read them and question whether any real, living person would feel such intense admiration for their work.

The author also shares a remark from a writer friend, who said the reason he knows the emails are fake is that the scammers have actually read all of his books. This observation underscores the unsettling level of detail in the fabricated fan mail.
summary: The novelist receives daily multi‑paragraph AI‑written emails that pose as fan mail and request a few hundred dollars to promote his work. When he accepted one sender’s offer to find new readers, the situation took a darker turn.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Inde Navarrette leads SNL's Halloween episode featuring David S. Pumpkins
content: Despite the odd stumble, the Oscar-tipped young actor helps to pull together the best episode of the season so far A new, spooktacular episode of Saturday Night Live kicks off at a Halloween-themed amusement park, where visitors cross paths with confusing “Halloween guy” David S Pumpkins (Tom Hanks) and his skeleton pals (Mikey Day and Bobby Moynihan). This seems like a copy-and-paste version of the previous Pumpkins sketches until Donald Trump (James Austin Johnson) jumps out to “[pause] SNL skit yet again.” He needles the live audience: “Aww, are you sad you don’t get to see your third David Pumpkin scene? I’ll save you three minutes; he keeps popping up and confusing people on the ride. The end!”
summary: A new spooktacular episode of Saturday Night Live takes place at a Halloween-themed amusement park with David S. Pumpkins (Tom Hanks) and skeleton pals (Mikey Day and Bobby Moynihan). Donald Trump (James Austin Johnson) interrupts the skit, teasing the audience about the recurring Pumpkin scene.
author: Guardian Culture

title: John Oliver Criticizes James Talarico Smears as Middle School Level Homophobia
content: The HBO host called out Trump’s ‘ridiculous’ stunts and Republican Islamophobia in the lead up to the US midterms On his HBO show on Sunday night, John Oliver focused on the last-minute rallies being held across the US leading up to the midterms. In Texas, Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton implored the few supporters assembled at a rally to not leave.
summary: John Oliver called out Trump’s stunts and Republican Islamophobia during his HBO show focused on midterms. He described the smears against James Talarico as middle school level homophobia.
author: Guardian Culture

title: ‘Screams on the level of a Taylor Swift concert’: horny romp Wicker gets the 4DX treatment
content:
Olivia Colman stars in the folk‑horror film Wicker, playing a woman who falls in love with a wicker man.  The movie’s steamy romance has prompted the question, “What does Olivia Colman’s hot sex with a basket tell us about heteropessimism?”  Colman herself noted, “I saw the script and went: oooh!”  She co‑stars with Alexander Skårsgard in the film.

Since its introduction in the United States in 2014, 4DX has been used mainly for action movies.  The format adds moving chairs, scent machines, wind and water sprayers, creating an experience that resembles an amusement‑park ride more than a traditional cinema.  4DX is the second‑most popular large premium format in the U.S., behind IMAX.

Wicker is an unexpected candidate for 4DX, following the 2024 release of Twisters, an action film about tornadoes that reached an “11/10” rating when paired with the format’s immersive effects.  The film’s use of 4DX is said to push the bounds of the format and enhance the sensorial joys of cinema.
summary: ‘Screams on the level of a Taylor Swift concert’: horny romp Wicker gets the 4DX treatment.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Michael Wilbon takes leave from ESPN's Pardon the Interruption for health issues
content: Pardon the Interruption co-host to take leave of absence Wilbon did not go into detail but cited ‘worrisome signs’ Michael Wilbon, the co-host of ESPN’s popular Pardon the Interruption talkshow alongside good friend Tony Kornheiser announced on Monday he is taking a leave of absence because of what he described as “multiple health issues”. Wilbon, who turns 68 later this month, wrote in a post on X that he is taking a trip to “the injured list” but added he hopes it is “not an extended one”.
summary: Michael Wilbon, co-host of ESPN's Pardon the Interruption, announced he is taking a leave of absence due to multiple health issues. He turns 68 later this month and said he hopes the leave will not be extended.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lions' Jack Campbell remains hospitalized after neck injury; initial signs positive
content:
The Detroit Lions announced that linebacker Jack Campbell, 26, will remain in hospital for the time being after suffering a neck injury during the team’s Sunday win over the Minnesota Vikings. The Lions said they will not release further information about his condition.

Initial signs are positive. Campbell was carted off the field and treated on the field for nine minutes after making a tackle. Players from both teams were visibly distraught as he received medical attention and was taken to a nearby facility for further treatment.
summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, 26, was carted off the field and taken to hospital after a neck injury during the win over the Minnesota Vikings. The team said initial signs are positive, but he will remain hospitalized for the time being and no further information will be released.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Glenn Maxwell Retires from Australia T20, Ends International Career
content:
Australian short‑form star Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from the international T20 arena, ending a career that saw him score 2,897 runs at an average of 28.97. The 38‑year‑old, who had already stepped away from one‑day internationals in 2025, will continue to play franchise cricket but will no longer represent Australia in T20 matches.

Maxwell also confirmed that his last game for Victoria, the state side, was the final chapter of his domestic career. He described the moment as unexpectedly emotional, saying he “got a little choked up” after telling teammates it would be his last state match. The announcement was made during an interview on The Final Word podcast.
summary: Glenn Maxwell, 38, has retired from Australia’s T20 team, ending his international career after scoring 2,897 runs at an average of 28.97. He previously retired from one-day internationals in 2025 and will continue to play franchise cricket.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alex Mitchell ruled out of England opener against Australia
content:
Alex Mitchell has been ruled out of England’s November opener against Australia on Sunday. The Northampton scrum‑half, who is the first‑choice No 9 under head coach Steve Borthwick, suffered a hamstring injury.  

Borthwick named the squad for the Wallabies match, with Bristol’s Harry Randall and Bath’s Ben Spencer called into the lineup.  

Mitchell sustained the hamstring damage during Northampton’s Premiership victory over Gloucester on Saturday and will have a scan on Tuesday to determine the injury’s extent.
summary: Alex Mitchell, Northampton scrum‑half, is ruled out of England’s opener against Australia. He suffered a hamstring injury during Northampton’s Premier League win over Gloucester and will have a scan on Tuesday.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carrick says he is not concerned about Martínez's attitude ahead of Roma match
content:
Michael Carrick has said he is not concerned about Lisandro Martínez’s attitude, despite the defender’s recent outburst aimed at the Manchester United hierarchy.  

Martínez was fined for comments about United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, and was sent off in the defeat against Chelsea at the weekend.  

He is expected to keep his place for the Champions League visit of Roma on Tuesday as United aim to end their worst run in 38 years, having failed to win any of their past nine matches.
summary: Michael Carrick says he is not concerned about Lisandro Martínez's attitude after Martínez's outburst and red card against Chelsea. Martínez is expected to keep his place for Manchester United's Champions League match against Roma, as the club seeks to end a nine‑game winless streak.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Revisiting the Superclásico: a story of death, violence, colour and family
content:
Attending the Boca v River match in the week I turned 60 prompted a lifetime of memories about the fixture. The Observer Sport Monthly had listed “Watch Boca Juniors Play River Plate in Buenos Aires” as No 1 on its 2004 list of 50 sporting things you must do before you die, cementing the derby’s place in the global imagination.

The article describes the derby’s reputation for colour, passion, and uncontainable emotion, noting the thump and thud of coordinated chants, shiny ticker‑tape amid flare smoke that matches the teams’ strips, and the concrete’s bounce as tens of thousands jump in unison. It also mentions mounted police surrounding the stadium, avalanche stoppers set alight, rockets aimed at players, and the presence of blood and fire.
summary: Revisiting the Superclásico: a story of death, violence, colour and family.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Everton beats Newcastle 1-0 with Thierno Barry goal as Jack Grealish returns
content: Jack Grealish will do well to get back into the Everton starting lineup when he returns to the squad – as David Moyes’s side are doing just fine without him. Newcastle were condemned to a second defeat in five days by Moyes’s young team, with a goal from Thierno Barry giving Everton victory against 10 men at St James’ Park.
summary: Newcastle lost 1-0 to Everton at St James’ Park, their second defeat in five days. Thierno Barry scored the only goal as Everton played with ten men, and Jack Grealish is expected to rejoin the squad.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Everton hold off Newcastle at St James' Park to rise to seventh
content: Everton secured a narrow victory over Newcastle United at St James’ Park, with Thierno Barry scoring his second goal against the hosts in five days. The win moved Everton up to seventh place in the Premier League table.
summary: Thierno Barry scored for Everton against Newcastle United, his second goal against them in five days. The narrow win at St James' Park moved Everton up to seventh place in the Premier League.

title: DOJ defends claim of 20,000 likely noncitizens on California voter rolls
content: The Department of Justice defended the accuracy of its claim that over 20,000 “likely noncitizens” are on California’s voter rolls. This defense came after an outside analysis indicated that more than 40 percent of the flagged names were not actually on the state’s voter rolls. DOJ officials addressed the discrepancy in a Sunday filing.
summary: DOJ says more than 20,000 likely noncitizens appear on California voter rolls. An outside analysis found that over 40% of names flagged as noncitizens were not on the state rolls.

title: Vladimir Putin’s Nov. 3 panic
content: President Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin are reportedly attempting to coerce Ukraine into unfavorable concessions ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. This pressure is being applied before a potential shift in congressional power occurs in January.

content: The Hill’s Decision Desk ’26: Election Night in America will air five hours of live coverage, moderated by Cory Smith and Drew Petrimoulx, with contributions from Chris Stirewalt and several special guests. The Hill, known as a comprehensive source of nonpartisan news covering politics and policy, will lead the broadcast.
summary: The Hill's Decision Desk '26 will provide five hours of live election coverage for Election Night in America. The program is moderated by Cory Smith and Drew Petrimoulx, with contributions from Chris Stirewalt and special guests.

title: Democrats urge IRS CEO to explain delayed tax gap data release
content: A group of Democratic lawmakers wrote to IRS CEO Frank Bisignano on Monday, urging him to explain why the agency has delayed publishing its tax‑gap estimate. The letter notes that the IRS has not yet released the data showing how much money owed by taxpayers was not paid on time.
summary: Democratic lawmakers urged IRS CEO Frank Bisignano to explain the delay in publishing the tax gap data. They wrote a letter on Monday asking why the agency has not yet released the information on unpaid taxpayer money.

title: Trump’s legacy at stake amid forecasted midterm blue wave
content: Forecasts of a midterm blue wave are said to put President Trump’s legacy on the line, as his political capital is viewed as vulnerable ahead of the elections. Trump has crisscrossed the country, holding 28 in‑person campaign rallies and a series of tele‑rallies, stopping in Republican strongholds such as Ohio, Texas, Iowa and Kansas.
summary: President Trump’s political capital is on the line as a potential blue wave threatens his final two years in office. He has crisscrossed the country, holding 28 in-person rallies and tele-rallies, stopping in Republican strongholds such as Ohio, Texas, Iowa, and Kansas.

title: Washoe County Mail Ballot Envelopes Contain 'FALSE' Printing Error
content: Thousands of voters in Washoe County, Nev., received mail‑in ballot return envelopes that had the word “FALSE” printed on them. A spokesperson for the county’s Registrar of Voters, George Guthrie, told The Hill that the envelopes were “not limited to voters of any particular political party.”
summary: Thousands of voters in Washoe County, Nev., received mail-in ballot return envelopes that had the word “FALSE” printed on them. County Registrar of Voters George Guthrie said the envelopes were not limited to voters of any particular political party.

title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Bid to Set Aside 20,000 California Ballots
content: The Supreme Court, in a one‑sentence order issued on Monday, rejected the Trump administration’s request to compel California officials to set aside 20,000 ballots it alleges belong to likely noncitizens and require investigation. The order contained no explanation and no noted dissents. California and immigration rights groups have questioned the authenticity of the administration’s list.
summary: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected the Trump administration’s effort to force California officials to set aside 20,000 ballots it claims belong to likely noncitizens and must be investigated. The court’s one‑sentence order contained no explanation and had no noted dissents.
author: The Hill

title: How National Guard units are being deployed around the midterm elections
content: National Guard members in at least seven states will play roles during Tuesday’s midterm elections. In Washington, plain‑clothes soldiers will help monitor ballot boxes in seven counties. In Iowa, guardsmen are assigned to monitor and defend election networks.
summary: How National Guard units are being deployed around the midterm elections.
author: The Hill

title: Supreme Court rejects DOJ request to intervene in California voter rolls dispute
content: The U.S. Supreme Court denied a last‑minute request from the Department of Justice to intervene in its ongoing dispute with California over the state’s voter rolls. The court’s decision effectively keeps the DOJ from stepping into the feud.
summary: Supreme Court rejects DOJ request to intervene in California voter rolls dispute.

title: Judge Accuses DOJ of Weaponization, Tosses Case Against Ex-FBI Officials
content: A judge accused the Department of Justice of weaponization and dismissed a case against former FBI officials. He said he was deeply troubled by the mistakes and rushed nature of the case concerning the FBI’s Hunter Biden probes, noting it was one of several politically charged DOJ actions before the midterms.
summary: The judge said he was deeply troubled by the mistakes and rushed nature of the case over the FBI's Hunter Biden probes. He tossed the case against ex-FBI officials, accusing the DOJ of weaponization.
author: NPR Politics

title: U.S. Research Finds Americans Overestimate Polarization, Majority Share Views
content: The United States has become more politically polarized, yet recent research indicates that many Americans overestimate the extent of these differences. The study finds a “messy middle” majority who share overlapping political views, suggesting that the nation’s divisions may not be as stark as commonly perceived.
summary: U.S. Research Finds Americans Overestimate Polarization, Majority Share Views.
author: NPR Politics

title: No10 defends Manchester flight to pick up Andy Burnham
content: Prime Minister’s office defended a flight to Manchester to pick up former city council leader Andy Burnham. Critics questioned the expense, but a No 10 spokesperson said that security, cost and operational requirements were all taken into account.
summary: No10 defended a flight to Manchester to collect Andy Burnham after backlash over its value for money. The office said security, cost and operational requirements were all taken into account.
author: BBC Politics

title: Scientists baffled by tender bond between bull Achille and donkey Patroclo
content:
Scientists report that a tender interspecies relationship between a bull named Achille and a donkey named Patroclo has provided new insights into social and sexual interactions among animals. The pair’s bond has been described as unusual, prompting researchers to examine how such relationships may inform broader understandings of animal behavior.

The study draws a parallel to the ancient myth of Achilles and Patroclus, whose intense friendship has been interpreted by some as a sexual relationship. By comparing the mythic narrative with the modern animal pairing, scientists suggest that the dynamics observed in the bull and donkey may illuminate similar patterns in other species.
summary: Scientists say the interspecies affair between bull Achille and donkey Patroclo sheds new light on social and sexual interactions between animals. The pair's tender bond has baffled scientists and prompted comparisons to the ancient myth of Achilles and Patroclus.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Britain’s 39m Smart Meters Transfer to Non‑Profit Startup
content:
Control of Britain’s 39 million smart meters has transferred to a non‑profit startup, ending a 13‑year licence held by Smart DCC, a subsidiary of Capita. The move follows years of spiralling costs and delays that plagued the network.  

The Capita‑owned company has pledged a “seamless transition” to its not‑for‑profit successor, which will assume responsibility for operating the data network that connects the meters starting this week.
summary: The handover ends Smart DCC's 13‑year licence, a Capita subsidiary, after spiralling costs and delays. The non‑profit startup will take over running the data network for Great Britain's 39m smart meters from this week, with Capita promising a seamless transition.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Vitamin C during pregnancy supports early brain development, study finds
content: A new study from Oregon Health & Science University reports that additional vitamin C intake during pregnancy supports early brain development. The research indicates that this low‑cost, accessible intervention can promote infant emotional well‑being.
summary: New research from Oregon Health & Science University shows that additional vitamin C intake during pregnancy can be an effective, low-cost and accessible intervention. The study indicates it promotes infant emotional well-being.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Body's failure to warn about pain when stepping into ice-cold lake
content: The piece examines the notion that when a person steps into an ice‑cold lake, the body could issue a polite warning about potential harm. It imagines a message such as, “Your feet may be at risk. Would you kindly consider stepping out?”
summary: When you step into an ice-cold lake, it would be nice if your body warned you about possible harm with a polite message: "Your feet may be at risk. Would you kindly consider stepping out?"
author: Medical Xpress

title: Choosing the Right Rehab Setting After Hospital Stay
content: After a hospital stay, patients who have suffered a broken hip, a stroke, or major surgery often need weeks of therapy to regain basic skills such as walking, dressing, or speaking again.
summary: The article discusses options for post-hospital rehabilitation, including inpatient rehab, nursing facilities, and home care. It notes that conditions such as broken hips, strokes, or major surgeries often require weeks of therapy to regain basic functions.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Innate immune protein regulates cholesterol and tumor growth, affecting cancer therapy
content: Scientists at the University of North Carolina Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center discovered an unexpected role for a key innate immune protein. The protein regulates cholesterol levels inside cells, influencing both tumor growth and how cancer responds to treatment. The findings illuminate how cancer cells rewire metabolism and suggest new therapeutic strategies.
summary: Scientists at the University of North Carolina Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center discovered an unexpected role for a key innate immune protein that regulates cholesterol levels inside cells. The protein also influences tumor growth and treatment response, pointing to potential new strategies for therapy.
author: Medical Xpress

title: CRELD1 protein links touch, temperature, pain, itch responses in mice
content: Researchers at Tsinghua University have identified a single protein that appears to influence several basic sensory responses in mice.  The team, led by Bailong Xiao, found that removing the protein CRELD1 weakened the animals’ reactions to touch, heat, cold, painful pressure and itch.  The study suggests that these distinct sensory pathways share a common molecular helper, raising the possibility that CRELD1 could serve as a new drug target for conditions involving touch, temperature, pain and itch.
summary: Researchers led by Bailong Xiao at Tsinghua University found that removing CRELD1 in mice weakens responses to touch, heat, cold, painful pressure, and itch. The protein appears to be a common molecular helper for these distinct sensory pathways.
author: Medical Xpress

title: No neuralyzer needed: Molecular pathways and circuits that trigger forgetting in C. elegans
content:
The 1997 film Men in Black introduced the neuralyzer, a handheld device that erases witnesses’ memories of extraterrestrial encounters. The device has become a cultural shorthand for instant forgetting.

Researchers have long sought to understand how and why humans remember and forget. As neuroscience has advanced, scientists are gradually uncovering the biological mechanisms that underlie memory, shedding light on the processes that allow memories to be formed and erased.
summary: The 1997 film Men in Black featured a neuralyzer that erased witnesses' memories. Researchers have slowly uncovered the biological mechanisms underlying memory, including the molecular pathways and circuits that trigger forgetting in C. elegans.
author: Medical Xpress

title: First-in-human trial of focused ultrasound to reduce schizophrenia hallucinations
content:
A first‑in‑human clinical trial using focused ultrasound to reduce hallucinations in schizophrenia has begun. The study targets patients who continue to hear voices despite antipsychotic treatment.  

Auditory hallucinations affect more than 70 % of people with schizophrenia, and roughly 40 % of those patients still experience persistent hallucinations. This underscores the urgent need for new therapeutic approaches.
summary: A first-in-human clinical trial will test focused ultrasound to reduce auditory hallucinations in schizophrenia. The trial targets patients who still experience persistent hallucinations despite antipsychotic medication.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Surge in Brain Connections Fine‑Tunes Visual Responses Within Days of Eyes Opening
content: A new study shows that the brain’s visual circuitry is first assembled by genetic programs before birth, then rapidly refined by visual experience after the eyes open. The research highlights how genes provide an initial blueprint, while subsequent sensory input fine‑tunes neural connections within days of eye opening.
summary: Brain wiring is shaped by both genes and experience, with the visual system serving as a model. Before the eyes open, genetic programs create a first draft of visual circuits, and after opening, visual experience refines that draft.
author: Medical Xpress

title: European flounder completes life cycle in freshwater
content: A recent study shows that European flounder can complete their entire life cycle in freshwater. Researchers sampled most flounders in Lake Pulmanki, northern Finland, and found they had spent their whole lives in the lake’s freshwater environment. This research, published in Evolution, is the first evidence of the species living entirely in freshwater.
summary: Most European flounders sampled in Lake Pulmanki, northern Finland, spent their entire lives in freshwater. This study, published in Evolution, provides the first evidence that the species can complete its whole life cycle in freshwater.
author: Phys.org

title: Trapped Light Triggers Magnetic Order in One-Dimensional Spin Chains, Study Finds
content:
A research team set out to clarify how inter‑particle forces within a material change under different conditions. They focused on one‑dimensional classical spin chains, which are arrays of magnetic particles that can be arranged linearly.

The team confined these spin chains inside a mirror‑box cavity illuminated by light. This setup forced the magnetic particles to organize themselves and triggered a phase transition—a change in the material’s collective state.

Their results provide the simplest exactly solvable examples that demonstrate how light can induce new phase transitions in materials, offering a clear illustration of light‑matter interaction in low‑dimensional systems.
summary: A research team discovered that confining one-dimensional classical spin chains inside a mirror box cavity with light forces the magnetic particles to organize and undergo a phase transition. Their work provides the simplest exactly solvable examples showing that light can create new phase transitions with materials.
author: Phys.org

title: Magnetic nanocomposites could shrink power components for computer chips
content:
Magnetic nanocomposites are being explored as a way to reduce the size of the components that supply power to computer chips.  

Researchers have shifted their focus from transistors to the hardware that delivers that power.  A chip requires electricity at the correct voltage and with fluctuations tightly controlled, and shrinking this hardware is a key challenge.  To address it, the team has fabricated tiny magnetic devices called stripline microinductors, which could help meet the voltage‑stability demands while reducing component size.
summary: Researchers built tiny stripline microinductors to deliver power to transistors with controlled voltage and reduced fluctuations. This approach aims to make the hardware that supplies power to transistors smaller.
author: Phys.org

title: Deep-sea mining impact on seafloor ecosystem still visible after 44 years
content: The article reports that the impact of deep‑sea mining on the seafloor ecosystem remains observable 44 years after initial disturbance. While scientific understanding of long‑term effects on the organic matter that sustains benthic life is limited, growing interest in extracting rare metals has heightened concerns that seabed disruption may affect deep‑ocean ecosystems.
summary: Little is known about the long-term effects of deep‑sea mining on the organic matter that supports life on the seafloor. Growing interest in mining the deep sea for rare metals has raised concern that disturbing the seabed could affect deep‑ocean ecosystems.
author: Phys.org

title: New diabetes implant uses electricity to lower blood sugar and promote weight loss
content: Researchers have created a new electronic implant that may change the treatment of type 2 diabetes. The device lowers blood sugar without using insulin or conventional drugs. It employs an electrically powered catalyst that converts excess glucose into a substance the body removes through urine, which could reduce the amount of energy stored as fat. title: Momentic Introduces Agents That Catch Bugs in Web, iOS, Android Apps
content:
Wei-Wei and Jeff, co-founders of Momentic, a Y Combinator W24 startup, have launched a suite of QA agents designed to autonomously plan, explore, and identify bugs in web, iOS, Android, and upcoming desktop applications. The founders, who previously worked on development tooling and infrastructure at companies including Robinhood, Retool, WeWork, and Qualtrics, developed the platform to address the inefficiencies of traditional testing frameworks like Playwright, Selenium, and Maestro. They argue that these existing tools require hardcoding implementation details and are misaligned with modern agentic software development life cycles, particularly as the adoption of coding agents increases the change failure rate.

Momentic’s core product, named Mo, is a custom agent harness built on three years of development and millions of test traces from real-world applications. The system utilizes a self-organizing agent graph that builds a directed acyclic graph during exploration, automatically forking large product areas into parallel sub-agents for concurrent execution. It employs specialized agents for domain-specific tasks, including planner agents that reason over screenshots and video, and locator agents that inspect page structure to resolve plain-English interaction targets. Additionally, the infrastructure supports cooperative resource leases, allowing multiple agents to coordinate when using or modifying overlapping resources, and includes a tunnel for exposing private sites and local apps to hosted agents.

In a benchmark comparing Mo against other coding agents on four open-source applications—Gitea, Metabase, Twenty, and Saleor—the startup reported that Mo achieved higher recall rates. The evaluation involved 1,396 human-labeled bugs, with each agent given the same brief and a fresh sandbox without source code access. In a time-boxed 60-minute run, Mo identified 269 bugs with an 84% precision rate and a 19.3% recall rate. By comparison, Codex found 86 bugs with 86% precision, Claude Code found 59 bugs with 80% precision, and Devin found 27 bugs with 84% precision. The cost per bug for Mo was $2.67, which is higher than Codex’s $0.80 but lower than Claude Code’s $4.09 and Devin’s $3.89.

The founders note that Mo’s performance scales with time, increasing its bug count by 52% between 30 and 60 minutes, whereas Codex saw only a 16% increase over the same period. While Mo prioritizes recall to find the most real bugs, they acknowledge that Codex is slightly more precise. The company has recently shipped PR testing capabilities for Vercel and Cloudflare deploy previews. New users are currently offered $250 in Mo spend, while paid plans provide higher infrastructure capacity and included usage options. The startup has published its results, write-up, dataset, and harness code for public review.
summary: Momentic, founded by Wei-Wei and Jeff, offers QA agents that autonomously explore and test web, iOS, Android, and upcoming desktop apps to catch bugs. In a 60‑minute benchmark, Mo detected 269 bugs with 19.3% recall and 84% precision, outperforming other agents.
