title: Ninja launches first Crispi Microwave with FusionCrisp technology, replacing two appliances
content: Ninja has introduced its first microwave, the Ninja Crispi Microwave, which uses FusionCrisp technology to deliver microwave‑quick cooking while producing the crispy texture typical of an air fryer, allowing it to serve the functions of both appliances.
summary: Ninja introduced its first Crispi Microwave, which uses FusionCrisp technology to blend microwave speed with air‑fryer crispness. The reviewer says the appliance replaced two of their kitchen devices at once.
author: TechCrunch

title: Top 12 autumn must‑have products from garlic press to vitamin C serum
content:
Autumn’s cooler weather has prompted many to turn to indoor comforts, with casserole dishes, electric heaters and hot coffee featuring prominently in recent shopping choices. The shift in temperature has also encouraged people to “hunker down” and consider using radiators or portable electric heaters to stay warm.

At the same time, shoppers are looking ahead to the party season and reviving parts of their wardrobes that have been out of use since early spring. Items highlighted include a clothes steamer for refreshing garments, a pencil skirt, a sheer silk shirt and a vitamin C serum aimed at maintaining skin glow throughout the winter months. These products were identified as some of the favourite October purchases.
summary: The article lists twelve products that readers are currently favoring for the autumn season. Items mentioned include a garlic press, a vitamin C serum, a clothes steamer, a pencil skirt, a silk shirt, casserole dishes and electric heaters.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Naomi Klein and Ilana Glazer call for blocking reckless AI IPOs and taxing billionaires
content: We cannot let the billionaire class take unprecedented risks with our future America is a divided country in crisis. Despite the sunny economic forecast coming from the Trump administration, millions of Americans are struggling to find and keep jobs, getting crushed under the rising cost of living, and losing health insurance when they need it the most. Meanwhile, via corporate consolidation and political corruption, the billionaire class is getting richer faster than ever before: a 40% increase in wealth in just the last two years. Today, the combined wealth of nearly 3,000 global billionaires equals one-fifth of the entire world’s yearly output. Nearly 1,000 billionaires live and do business in the United States.
summary: Naomi Klein and Ilana Glazer call for blocking reckless AI IPOs and taxing billionaires.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Palantir AI platform claimed beneficial by 29 NHS trusts but many not using it
content: Exclusive: Gap between NHS claim and trusts’ comments described as ‘very misleading’ by senior health official More than two dozen hospital trusts the NHS claims have benefited from Palantir’s medical data platform are not using all or most of the AI-powered technology, the Guardian can reveal. The 29 hospital trusts that NHS England publicly lists as “realising benefits” from the controversial £330m federated data platform (FDP) have said the system is not live or they are not using any of its applications. The apparent gap between the NHS claim and the trusts’ understanding was described as “very misleading” by one senior health official.
summary: Palantir AI platform claimed beneficial by 29 NHS trusts but many not using it.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Prospect union to organise 7,000 Google UK workers after new union access rights
content: Trade unions are set to expand their presence in UK big‑tech firms after new employment‑rights legislation allowing union access to workplaces took effect. On Monday, Google UK signed an agreement with the Prospect union under which the union will hold workplace sessions and recruit members. The deal covers roughly 7,000 Google employees in the United Kingdom, including staff at YouTube, while workers at DeepMind are excluded from the arrangement.
summary: The Prospect union has reached an agreement with Google UK to organise about 7,000 workers across its UK operations, including YouTube but excluding DeepMind. The deal follows new UK employment rights that give unions workplace access, enabling further inroads into big‑tech firms.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Investors withdraw $3.6bn from Binance after $6.3bn hack linked to North Korea
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has started to permit withdrawals after a theft that experts believe originated in North Korea. The platform was hit on Thursday by a $6.3 billion theft, which has been described as the biggest heist in history. In response, investors have moved $3.6 billion (£2.7 billion) out of Binance as the exchange works to recover from the record hack. Experts have identified North Korea as the probable source of the theft.
summary: Investors withdraw $3.6bn from Binance after $6.3bn hack linked to North Korea.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Mbappé apologises after meme likening him to Mao, three Chinese firms end deals
content: Kylian Mbappé issued an apology after his remarks about a meme that portrayed him as Chinese leader Mao Zedong provoked backlash in China. The dispute led at least three Chinese companies to terminate brand agreements with the footballer, and it prompted a response from China’s Foreign Ministry.
summary: Kylian Mbappé apologized after remarks about a meme depicting him as Chinese leader Mao Zedong sparked backlash in China. At least three Chinese companies have ended brand deals with him, and the controversy prompted a response from China's Foreign Ministry.
author: Euronews

title: Iran says it can reopen Hormuz in two days if US meets conditions
content: Iran announced it could reopen the Hormuz Strait within two days if the United States meets its conditions. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the revised timeline, shortened from a seven‑day proposal in September, reflects Iran’s good‑faith approach, but added that the outcome depends on Washington.
summary: Iran says it can reopen Hormuz within two days if the United States meets its conditions. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the timeline was shortened from a seven‑day proposal in September and that everything depends on Washington.
author: Euronews

title: Cyberattack disables refrigeration in Belgian supermarkets, fridges left empty
content: Supermarkets in Belgium and other European countries have reported cyberattacks that targeted refrigeration systems. The attacks caused food to spoil and forced some stores to shut down their fridges and freezers, leaving the refrigeration areas empty.
summary: Supermarkets in several European countries reported cyberattacks that targeted refrigeration systems. The attacks caused food to spoil and forced some stores to close off their fridges and freezers.
author: Euronews

title: Italy has most journalists under police protection as threats increase
content: Italy has the highest number of journalists under police protection in Europe, reflecting a profession that faces frequent threats and intimidation. While the European Union has introduced measures intended to safeguard press freedom, the implementation of those protections is proceeding slowly.
summary: Italy has the largest number of journalists under police protection in Europe. Journalism in Italy is especially vulnerable to threats and intimidation, and EU measures to protect press freedom are being implemented slowly.
author: France 24

title: Fridge cyberattacks cause temperature spikes in supermarkets across five European countries
content: Stores and supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Finland, Estonia and Sweden reported abrupt temperature spikes in their fridges and freezers early Monday, which they attribute to an apparent cyberattack on refrigeration units. The incidents come after a comparable attack in October that affected hundreds of French supermarkets and resulted in food loss and fires.
summary: Stores and supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Finland, Estonia and Sweden reported abrupt temperature spikes in their fridges and freezers early Monday in an apparent cyberattack targeting refrigeration units. The incidents follow a similar attack that hit hundreds of supermarkets across France in October, triggering food loss and fires.
author: France 24

title: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over Abdul El‑Sayed
content: France 24’s Fraser Jackson previewed the political landscape one day before the United States’ midterm elections, noting that both Democrats and Republicans were making their final appeals to voters. In Michigan, Democrat Haley Stevens drew attention by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers over the Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed. Stevens had previously lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to El‑Sayed in a contested race, and her cross‑party endorsement prompted accusations that she was acting out of “sour grapes.”
summary: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic candidate Abdul El‑Sayed in the state’s Senate race. She had lost the Michigan Democrats’ Senate primary to El‑Sayed, leading some to accuse her of sour grapes.
author: France 24

title: French high school protests resume Monday, targeting schools in Paris, Marseille, Rennes
content: French high‑school student protests resumed on Monday after a two‑week autumn break, but on a much smaller scale than in recent weeks. Pupils attempted to blockade a handful of high schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes.
summary: French high school student protests resumed on Monday after a two‑week break. Pupils tried to blockade a few high schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes on a much smaller scale than in past weeks.
author: France 24

title: Argentina's President Milei eyes Patagonia as site for new data centres
content: Argentina’s President Javier Milei is advocating for an increase in data‑centre construction, and the government has identified the open steppes of Patagonia as a potentially suitable location. This follows broader global concerns about data‑centres’ noise, high power use and visual impact.
summary: Citizens and lawmakers worldwide are pushing back against data centre construction due to noise, power consumption and visual impact. President Javier Milei wants more data centres in Argentina and the government sees Patagonia's open steppes as a potential location.
author: France 24

title: Democrats eye Michigan Senate seat as Gen Z backs Abdul El‑Sayed
content: Michigan’s Senate seat is described as a must‑win for the Democratic Party as it aims to gain control of the U.S. Senate. Progressive candidate Abdul El‑Sayed is reported to have a surge of energy behind him, particularly among younger voters, prompting questions about whether Gen Z enthusiasm will translate into votes and help Democrats secure the seat.
summary: Michigan’s Senate seat is a must‑win for the Democratic Party as it seeks to take control of the Senate. Progressive candidate Abdul El‑Sayed is seeing a surge of energy from younger voters.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine and Russia emergency alert apps hit by cyberattacks sending fake warnings
content: Authorities in Ukraine and Russia reported that cyberattacks compromised their emergency‑alert mobile applications. In Ukraine, users received false warnings of an imminent nuclear threat, while Moscow said hackers accessed the Russian Emergency Situations Ministry’s app to send fake alerts and are working to restore its functionality.
summary: Authorities in Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert mobile apps were targeted by cyberattacks, with Ukrainian users receiving false warnings of an imminent nuclear threat. Moscow said hackers accessed the Russian Emergency Situations Ministry’s app to send fake alerts and that work was underway to restore its functionality.
author: France 24

title: Richard Johnson says Trump’s unpopularity threatens Republicans in 2026 midterms
content: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections. Far from assuming that Trump's formidable campaigning instincts can once again mobilize Republican voters, Johnson questions whether the president's political influence has become a liability for the very party he once transformed. He points to a potentially significant realignment within the American electorate. Economic grievances, rising living costs, trade disputes and disillusionment with the war in Iran appear, in Johnson's reading, to be weakening important elements of the coalition that sustained Trump's return to power. Particularly consequential is the possibility that Latino voters, agricultural communities and sections of the MAGA electorate may be reconsidering their political loyalties or withdrawing from electoral participation altogether.
summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections.
author: France 24

title: Nine dead as Learjet crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida
content:
A Learjet crashed near a busy road in a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach County, Florida.  

The crash killed all nine people on board and left a large crater on the ground.
summary: A Learjet crashed near a busy road in a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach County. All nine people on board were killed and the impact left a large crater in the ground.
author: DW World

title: Democrats pivot climate messaging to lower electricity bills
content: Recent Democratic campaign messaging has shifted away from climate‑change themes toward pledges to reduce electricity costs for voters. While the party’s current focus emphasizes lower energy bills, observers note the unanswered question of what specific climate actions Democrats would pursue if they gain control of Congress.
summary: Climate change has largely vanished from Democrats' campaign pitches, which now emphasize promises to lower electricity bills. The article questions what climate actions the party would pursue if it gains control of Congress.
author: DW World

title: Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia threatens investment and public finances
content: Ethiopia’s economy is currently expanding robustly. However, renewed fighting in the country’s northern region—a BRICS member—raises concerns that the conflict could deter investment, strain public finances and increase the cost of living.
summary: Ethiopia's economy is growing strongly. Renewed fighting in the north could deter investment, strain public finances and push up the cost of living.
author: DW World

title: Ryanair mulls pay freezes, risking union clash amid soaring fuel costs
content: Ryanair has announced that it is considering a pay freeze for its staff, a move that could lead to a confrontation with unions as the airline seeks to offset soaring fuel costs linked to the Middle East conflict. In addition to the proposed wage hold, the carrier is weighing reductions in crew numbers on flights and a greater reliance on artificial intelligence as part of its broader cost‑cutting strategy. These measures reflect Ryanair’s effort to manage rising operating expenses.
summary: Ryanair is considering implementing pay freezes, which could spark a confrontation with unions as it seeks to offset soaring fuel costs driven by the Middle East conflict. The airline is also weighing reductions in crew numbers on flights and increased use of AI as part of its cost‑cutting drive.
author: Guardian World

title: Supermarket freezers in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg rise overnight in suspected hack
content:
Supermarket chains across Europe have reported that the temperatures in refrigerators and freezers rose overnight, raising concerns of a second suspected cyber‑attack. The incident, affecting stores in Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg, mirrors a previous hack that caused significant food losses in France.

In Sweden, the Coop chain confirmed that six of its outlets were impacted, while ICA noted that a limited number of its stores experienced an overnight incident that disrupted their refrigeration and freezer systems. The companies have not yet identified the cause but are investigating the disruptions.
summary: Supermarket chains in Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg said refrigerator and freezer temperatures rose overnight, raising fears of a cyber‑attack similar to the one that hit French stores. Sweden’s Coop reported six stores were affected, and ICA said it was aware a limited number of stores experienced an incident that impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems.
author: Guardian World

title: Ikea and other European shops hit by fridge cyber‑hacks
content:
Supermarkets across Europe have reported meddling with temperature‑control systems, and Ikea is listed among the shops affected by fridge‑related cyber‑hacks, according to Europe live.

title: RBA expected to deliver fifth rate hike, warning of sharper, longer slowdown
content: Australia’s central bank expected to hit mortgage holders again on Tuesday, as war in Middle East combines with collapsing house prices Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Australia’s economy is set for a “sharper, longer slowdown”, major bank economists say, as the Reserve Bank is forced to keep interest rates higher to rid the nation of persistent inflationary pressures. The RBA is widely expected to hit mortgage holders with a fifth rate hike on Tuesday, in a move that will push the cash rate to its highest since 2008 amid rising worries the economy could even be tipped into recession.
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is widely expected to raise the cash rate for a fifth time on Tuesday, targeting mortgage borrowers and pushing the rate to its highest since 2008. Major bank economists say the economy is heading for a sharper, longer slowdown with growing worries it could slip into recession.

title: Award‑winning Australian children’s author Craig Silvey jailed over child exploitation material
content:
Award‑winning Australian author Craig Silvey, known for the novel Jasper Jones, was sentenced to seven months in prison by a Western Australian district court. The court heard that Silvey had sent multiple messages expressing a sexual desire for young boys and had been caught in possession of explicit images of children and adults.

Silvey pleaded guilty earlier this year to charges of distributing and possessing child exploitation material. The sentence, announced on Monday, reflects the seriousness of the offenses and the court’s decision to impose a custodial term.
summary: Craig Silvey, the award‑winning Australian author of Jasper Jones, sent multiple messages expressing sexual desire for young boys and was found with explicit images of children and adults. He pleaded guilty to distributing and possessing child exploitation material and was sentenced on Monday to seven months in prison.
author: Guardian World

title: Reddit and Digital Freedom Project take under-16 social media ban to High Court
content:
Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project, an advocacy group led by New South Wales state MP John Ruddick, will ask the High Court to overturn Australia’s under‑16s social‑media ban. The challengers argue the law infringes the implied freedom of political communication.

The ban, introduced nearly 11 months ago, requires ten platforms—Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Kick, X, Twitch and Threads—to deactivate or suspend accounts of users they determine to be under 16 years old. The upcoming court case will be the first major legal test of the legislation.
summary: Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project, led by NSW state MP John Ruddick, are challenging Australia’s under‑16 social media ban in the High Court. The ban, introduced nearly 11 months ago, required ten platforms including Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Kick, X, Twitch and Threads to deactivate or suspend accounts of users under 16.
author: Guardian World

title: Shoalhaven council blocks Phil Buehler's 'Wall of Tears' over safety concerns
content: Exclusive: Shoalhaven council says Wall of Tears installation by Phil Buehler posed risk to staff, visitors and tenants Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A New South Wales local council has refused to show a world-renowned artwork about children killed in Gaza after asking organisers to investigate hiring “armed guards” to counter the risk of “community conflict” over the mural. The group, Shoalhaven Friends of Palestine, was aiming to show the Wall of Tears installation by American artist Phil Buehler at the Shoalhaven Regional Gallery in Nowra on Tuesday, following the work being exhibited around Australia, including on the front lawns of Parliament House in Canberra in September.
summary: Shoalhaven council said the Wall of Tears installation by American artist Phil Buehler posed a risk to staff, visitors and tenants. The council refused to show the artwork at Shoalhaven Regional Gallery in Nowra after asking Shoalhaven Friends of Palestine to investigate hiring armed guards to counter community conflict risk.
author: Guardian World

title: Guardian Essential poll finds record low interest in Melbourne Cup, 9% high interest
content: Growing disdain for gambling and animal cruelty concerns drive sliding interest in race that once ‘stopped the nation’ Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne Cup, with more than two-thirds surveyed saying they have low or zero interest in the annual horse race. Support for the Melbourne Cup has been sliding consistently for a number of years, but the Guardian Essential poll found just 9% of Australians said they had high interest in the race now – nearly half the proportion in 2025.
summary: A Guardian Essential poll found a record number of Australians have low or zero interest in the Melbourne Cup, with more than two‑thirds surveyed expressing little interest. Only 9% said they had high interest in the race, about half the proportion reported in 2025.
author: Guardian World

title: Kangaroos face internal threat as Rugby League World Cup knockout stage begins
content:
The Rugby League World Cup has entered its knockout phase, and Australia’s national side, the Kangaroos, sit atop the competition with three wins from three matches. While the team has struggled to overcome the errors and disconnection of its first two games, it remains the front‑runner and is pursuing the trophy for a fourth consecutive tournament in front of home supporters.

Three remaining opponents are set to test the Kangaroos, yet the article notes a growing sense of unease, suggesting that the most significant threat may arise from within the Australian camp itself.
summary: The Kangaroos have won three of three matches and are pursuing a fourth consecutive Rugby League World Cup title. As the tournament reaches the knockout stage, the team faces a potential internal threat despite upcoming tests from three remaining opponents.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia rests Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood for England ODIs and T20s
content:
Australia’s one‑day and T20 squads for the upcoming series against England will not include Test captain Pat Cummins, nor fast‑bowling partners Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. The trio were omitted from both the three‑ODI and five‑T20 international squads announced on Monday, with officials saying the rest will help them prepare for a demanding schedule of ten Tests in fourteen weeks this summer.

The England side is set to introduce debutants Beardman and Shaw as the series approaches.
summary: Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood will be rested for Australia's upcoming one‑day and T20 series against England. The trio were omitted from the ODI and T20 squads announced on Monday as part of a refresh ahead of a demanding summer Test schedule.
author: Guardian Sport

content: BBC Sport’s Kelly Cates and Micah Richards noted that Declan Rice has become a rounded presence in Arsenal’s midfield. Former player Danny Murphy added that, were Rice more selfish, he would likely increase his goal tally.

title: Fast ferries threaten endangered Mediterranean whales despite speed‑limit recommendation
content:
A Guardian investigation has found that, despite a recommendation to slow down, leading shipping companies continue to travel above advised speeds in a key habitat for cetaceans. This occurs in the north‑western Mediterranean, a region critical for marine mammals.

Marine biologist Alice Barbarioli waits with her camera trained on the horizon. A hydrophone beneath the Pelagos research vessel detected codas – the sequence of clicks sperm whales use to communicate. The vessel is located in the Pelagos sanctuary, a conservation area established to protect marine mammals.

The sperm whale reveals its head and dorsal fin to those onboard, and the crew rushes to take photos and note the rhythm of its breathing. After a few minutes, the animal arches its back and heads back into the depths, while observers wait to catch a glimpse of its tail.
summary: Fast ferries threaten endangered Mediterranean whales despite speed‑limit recommendation.

title: UN report warns permanent cryosphere damage if world overshoots 1.5°C
content:
A UN‑backed report warns that even brief temperature rises above the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C target could cause lasting harm to glaciers and polar ice sheets. The assessment says Earth’s icy regions are experiencing dangerous melting and that global heating must be reduced to below 1 °C after any inevitable period of overshoot.

The report also notes that permanent, widespread loss of snow and ice undermines a “persistent myth” that exceeding the 1.5 °C limit—reaching 2 °C or 3 °C—might be manageable or even preferable to immediate emissions cuts.
summary: A UN‑backed report says even temporary rises above the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C target could cause permanent harm to glaciers and polar ice sheets. It adds that global heating must be brought back below 1°C after any overshoot and rejects the notion that overshooting to 2°C or 3°C is manageable.

content: A recent study found that one blood protein outperformed the other 29 biomarkers evaluated for assessing metabolic dysfunction‑associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Accurate assessment of MASLD is essential for staging the condition, selecting appropriate therapies and tracking treatment response, a process that has traditionally relied on invasive liver‑biopsy sampling.
summary: A single blood protein was identified as the most effective among 30 tests for evaluating MASLD. Assessment of the disease has often required an invasive liver biopsy to obtain tissue for examination.

title: MIT engineers develop water‑resistant microneedle vaccine system for farmed fish
content:
Fish raised in pools and ponds now supply a growing share of the world’s protein, but disease outbreaks can cause major losses for aquaculture producers.  Today’s most effective vaccination method for fish relies on metal needles, a process that requires sedating the fish, removing them from the water, and having workers inject each animal individually.  The technique is described as labor‑intensive, costly, stressful for fish, and risky for workers because of rapid handling, potential cross‑contamination and accidental needle sticks.

A team of researchers from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the U.S. Department of Agriculture has introduced an alternative delivery platform that uses water‑resistant, food‑grade microneedles.  The microneedles are fabricated from silk fibroin and coated with a thin layer of shellac, an insect‑secreted resin commonly used in food coatings and pills.  This coating creates a moisture barrier that allows the microneedles to remain attached to fish skin, penetrate lightly, and then decompose after delivering their cargo.  The researchers reported that the system can store and release a range of vaccines, including bacterial vaccines and DNA plasmid vaccines, with release times that can be tuned from minutes to up to 24 hours.

The study, published in ACS Nano, demonstrated the technology on rainbow trout as small as one to two grams.  According to Gregory Wiens of the USDA National Center for Cool and Cold Water Aquaculture, the microneedles can pierce wet skin, stay attached while the fish swim, and release either bacterin or DNA vaccines in a controlled manner.  Laboratory tests showed that the microneedles preserved about half of the DNA plasmids’ structure after four weeks of dry storage, a feature the authors note could ease the need for cold‑chain logistics in rural aquaculture settings.

The work builds on prior silk microneedle research led by Benedetto Marelli, a professor in MIT’s Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering.  Marelli’s lab received support from the Abdul Latif Jameel Water and Food Systems Lab (J‑WAFS) and, beginning in 2022, biomedical engineer Meng Li joined the project.  Li, a postdoctoral researcher and first author of the paper, secured a USDA fellowship in 2024 that provided additional funding and connections, including access to a DNA vaccine for rainbow trout from the U.S. Geological Survey.

While the authors acknowledge that further development is needed before large‑scale farm deployment, they present the microneedle platform as a potentially safer and more efficient tool for vaccinating small fish, improving worker safety, and supporting the broader goal of expanding sustainable aquaculture production.  The research was funded in part by MIT’s J‑WAFS and the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
summary: Fish that are cultivated in pools or ponds are an increasingly important source of food around the world. Unfortunately, disease outbreaks can cause substantial losses in aquaculture.

title: Jackery launches Explorer 100D, its smallest portable power station at 1.87 lb
content:
Jackery announced a new portable power station that uses lithium iron‑phosphate (LFP) batteries, the same battery chemistry the company first introduced in 2023. The Explorer 100D is described as Jackery’s smallest power station to date, measuring 4.6 × 3.4 × 3.4 inches and weighing 1.87 pounds, with a 96 Wh (30,000 mAh) capacity that can power multiple devices on a long flight.

The Explorer 100D will be sold through Walmart beginning November 15 for $99, and it is already available at Costco for customers who do not wish to wait.
summary: Jackery launches Explorer 100D, its smallest portable power station at 1.87 lb.
author: The Verge

title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion after Max Verstappen wins Mexico City GP
content: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 world champion, a milestone achieved after finishing third in the Mexico City Grand Prix. The 20‑year‑old trailed Max Verstappen, who won the race, and Lewis Hamilton. Antonelli’s podium finish secured the championship title.
summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, 20, became the youngest Formula 1 world champion. He finished third in the Mexico City Grand Prix behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.
author: Euronews

title: Iran warns a new war with the US could outlast the previous conflict
content: Iran warned on Sunday that a renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous conflict. President Donald Trump said Washington still had targets to strike, and Tehran responded that any retaliation would have no geographical limits. Diplomatic efforts continued as officials sought to prevent a fresh escalation before Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections.
summary: Iran warned on Sunday that a renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous conflict, after President Donald Trump suggested Washington still had targets to strike. Tehran said retaliation would have no geographical limits while diplomatic efforts continued to avert escalation ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections.
author: France 24

title: Halloween weekend shootings across US kill at least six, dozens injured, Dallas worst
content: Over Halloween weekend, shootings in nightlife districts and near university campuses across the United States left at least six people dead and dozens wounded, with Dallas reporting the highest toll. Police are investigating multiple incidents in several states, and some suspects remain at large.
summary: A spate of shootings in nightlife districts and near university campuses across the United States over Halloween weekend left at least six people dead and dozens wounded. Dallas recorded the highest toll, and police are investigating multiple incidents in several states while some suspects remain at large.
author: France 24

title: Russia and Ukraine blame each other for hacking emergency alert apps
content: Russia and Ukraine have each accused the other of hacking their emergency‑alert applications. The accusations surfaced after a local ceasefire in the war’s eastern Kherson region expired on Sunday. Both sides warned of renewed fighting, and Kyiv indicated it could pause strikes on Russian oil refineries in return for U.S. Patriot missiles.
summary: Russia and Ukraine accused each other of hacking their emergency alert applications as a local ceasefire in the war's eastern Kherson region expired on Sunday. The cyberattacks came as both sides warned of renewed fighting and Kyiv signalled it could halt strikes on Russian oil refineries in exchange for US Patriot missiles.
author: France 24

title: Trump calls Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed a “jihadist” at Iowa rally
content: President again took aim at progressive Senate candidate and lauded Haley Stevens for endorsing Mike Rogers Donald Trump railed against Democratic US senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed at a campaign event in Iowa Sunday, repeatedly referring to the Michigan progressive as a “jihadist”. Trump’s comments aimed to influence a neck-and-neck race that will play an outsized role in determining which party controls the senate after Tuesday’s midterm elections.
summary: Trump calls Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed a “jihadist” at Iowa rally.
author: Guardian World

title: UK Parliament report says Britain lacks coherent China policy, risks US or Beijing sway
content: Commons committee says lack of coherent strategy is hampering business and leaving national security risks unaddressed The UK is making up policy on China “as it goes along” and risks having its strategy dictated by Washington or Beijing, a parliamentary report has concluded. An investigation by the Commons business, innovation, science and trade select committee said Labour’s failure to formulate a coherent strategy since 2024 “combined the worst of both worlds” for the UK in relation to China.
summary: UK Parliament report says Britain lacks coherent China policy, risks US or Beijing sway.
author: Guardian World

title: Counsellors and psychotherapists urge UK statutory regulation in landmark report
content:
Professional bodies have issued a report urging UK ministers to introduce statutory regulation for counsellors and psychotherapists. The report argues that such regulation would boost public confidence and protect people from abuse. It describes the call for regulation as a “watershed moment” for the profession.

The document notes that, unlike most other healthcare roles such as doctors, midwives and osteopaths, the titles “psychotherapist” and “counsellor” are currently neither protected nor statutorily regulated in the United Kingdom.
summary: Professional bodies say ministers should introduce statutory regulation for counsellors and psychotherapists to protect the public from abuse, calling the report a watershed moment. The report notes that, unlike doctors, midwives and osteopaths, the titles “psychotherapist” and “counsellor” are not protected or statutorily regulated in the UK.
author: Guardian World

title: Spain high-speed train crash kills 69, including US, Japan, Canada citizens
content:
Spanish authorities said a high‑speed train collision last week killed 69 people, making it one of Europe’s deadliest rail incidents of the century. Among the dead were 54 Spaniards, four U.S. citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic.

Relatives of the victims are waiting for forensic teams to identify the deceased, a process that sometimes involves examining individual body parts, officials added. The casualty figures and nationalities were confirmed by authorities following the crash.
summary: Spain high-speed train crash kills 69, including US, Japan, Canada citizens.
author: Guardian World

title: WA police facial recognition trial scans over 1.3 million faces, leads to 122 arrests
content:
Western Australian police completed a five‑month trial of real‑time facial‑recognition technology that scanned 1,380,882 faces. The system was deployed in 100 surveillance vans across 43 regional and metropolitan locations, concluding on Saturday.

The trial produced 122 arrests and led officers to engage with 146 registered sex offenders. It also generated nine false alerts, highlighting the technology’s potential for incorrect identifications.
summary: During a five‑month trial, Western Australia police used real‑time facial recognition in 100 deployments across 43 regional and metropolitan locations, scanning 1,380,882 faces. The trial, which ended on Saturday, led to 122 arrests and nine false alerts.
author: Guardian World

title: Darwin's Matthew Maurice lands $1 million barramundi on night trip with brother
content:
A 26‑year‑old Darwin resident, Matthew Maurice, became $1 million richer after catching an 80‑centimetre, red‑tagged barramundi during a night‑time fishing trip with his brother. The catch was part of a Northern Territory competition, and Maurice said, “I’m just happy to catch fish,” after landing the fish.

Maurice had finished football training and, on Thursday evening, set out on a boat with his sibling, who was visiting from overseas. The 80‑centimetre barramundi was the prize that earned him the million‑dollar reward.
summary: Matthew Maurice, a 26‑year‑old Darwin man, caught an 80 cm red‑tagged barramundi worth $1 million during a Northern Territory competition. He was fishing at night on a Thursday evening with his brother, who was visiting from overseas, after finishing football training.

content: Judicial commission finds against Vicky Prapas over a series of comments, including one made when school children were present Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A magistrate who told a court user “I want to slap you around a bit, too” has come under fire for her offensive and inappropriate language. title: Mbappé penalty fuels Real Madrid's 3-0 win, sixth straight victory
content:
Kylian Mbappé ended a turbulent week by scoring a penalty that secured a 3‑0 victory for Real Madrid over Racing Santander on Sunday. The French forward had just missed out on the Ballon d’Or, losing to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane, and later issued an apology after a social‑media backlash over a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Separately, Bellingham and Diomandé were credited with a 3‑0 win for their side against Racing Lazio in Serie A, a result that followed a comeback victory over Cagliari.
summary: Kylian Mbappé scored a penalty as Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0, extending their winning streak to six games. The French forward had recently lost the Ballon d’Or to Harry Kane and apologized for a video that joked about Mao Zedong.

title: Arsenal beat Liverpool to move three points clear at top of table
content: Afternoon began with talk of a title bid, but Arsenal looked more and more comfortable as the second half wore on Andoni Iraola had swatted aside any question that veered in the direction of Liverpool’s title credentials during his press conference on Friday with two simple words. “Too early,” he would respond. The Liverpool head coach was dismissive in terms of the stage of the season but, as Arsenal doggedly demonstrated, too early also applies to the development of his team. Arsenal cavorted to the sound of fury at Anfield. At the final whistle Mikel Arteta leapt into the arms of the first-team coach Gabriel Heinze as he celebrated the release of his first win at Liverpool as Arsenal manager, his club’s first league victory at Anfield in 14 years and the champions moving three points clear at the top of the table. His players, tireless in the protection of Kai Havertz’s early winner, lined up to accept the acclaim from a jubilant away section. Anger filled the space around them.
summary: Mikel Arteta secured his first win at Liverpool as Arsenal manager, marking the champions' first league victory at Anfield in 14 years. The result moved Arsenal three points clear at the top of the table, while Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola had previously described the team's title bid as too early.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sheila Chepkirui Wins Second NYC Marathon; Almgren Takes Men's Debut Title
content:
Sweden’s Andreas Almgren claimed the men’s title at the New York City Marathon on Sunday in his debut over the 26.2-mile distance. After a career focused on half marathons and the 10,000m, Almgren pulled away from Italy’s Yemaneberhan Crippa in the final mile to finish in two hours, six minutes, and one second. Crippa placed second, 13 seconds behind, while Lesotho’s Kamohelo Mofolo finished third, edging out defending champion Benson Kipruto.

In the women’s race, Kenya’s Sheila Chepkirui secured her second title. The United States’ Jessica McClain finished in second place.
summary: Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women's race of the New York City Marathon for the second time. Sweden's Andreas Almgren claimed the men's title on his debut, finishing in 2:06:01 after pulling away from Yemaneberhan Crippa, who finished 13 seconds behind, with Kamohelo Mofolo of Lesotho taking third place over defending champion Benson Kipruto.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cardinals beat Cowboys in OT after Minshew heroics; Jackson needs thumb surgery
content:
Gardner Minshew’s heroics inspired the Arizona Cardinals to a wild victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. After missing a PAT that would have won the game with six seconds left in regulation, Chad Ryland kicked a winning 42-yard field goal in overtime. The Cardinals defeated Dallas for the fifth consecutive time, improving to 5-0 at AT&T Stadium, the Cowboys’ home venue that opened in 2009.

In related news, Lamar Jackson requires surgery on an injured thumb, which could end his season.
summary: The Arizona Cardinals defeated the Dallas Cowboys in overtime after Chad Ryland kicked a winning 42-yard field goal. Lamar Jackson requires surgery on an injured thumb, which could end his season.

title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GP
content:
Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest driver to claim the Formula One world championship, securing the title with a third-place finish at the Mexican Grand Prix. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver clinched the crown with four races remaining in the season, marking his debut F1 title. By achieving this feat, Antonelli also became the first Italian to win the championship since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

The race itself was won by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who finished ahead of Lewis Hamilton in second place. Hamilton’s teammate, Charles Leclerc, crossed the line in fourth position. The result represented a significant milestone for the Mercedes team, as it is their first drivers’ championship since Hamilton’s final victory in 2020 and the team’s 10th overall in the sport’s history.
summary: Kimi Antonelli, 20, clinched the Formula One world championship by finishing third in the Mexican Grand Prix, securing the title with four races remaining. He became the youngest driver to win the championship and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari, while Mercedes claimed its first drivers’ championship since Hamilton in 2020.

title: PolyU develops Tumour Heterogeneity Index to predict breast cancer AKT inhibitor response
content:
Researchers at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) have created an imaging biomarker called the Tumour Heterogeneity Index (THI). The THI allows a noninvasive assessment of breast cancer patients’ likely response to AKT inhibitors before treatment begins, enabling clinicians to identify those most likely to benefit.

In a study, patients with a high THI had an estimated pathological complete response (pCR) rate of 56.1%, markedly higher than patients with a low THI. The technology could help patients receive the most appropriate treatment earlier, reduce unnecessary side effects, and allow clinicians to better tailor treatment strategies to individual patients.

The victory came just 534 days after the team’s inaugural game, a record that underscores the rapid rise of the franchise.

The championship roster included a point guard who had been dismissed by Dallas, a starting forward who had been waived five times, and a late‑blooming All‑Star who had been overlooked by every league team. These overlooked players found a coach who had built a career on making small openings count. Natalie Nakase, who earned a scholarship at UCLA from a walk‑on spot and secured a coaching position in Japan’s top men’s league after sending an unsolicited scouting report, brought a unique blend of trust and opportunity to the team.

Nakase’s circuitous journey taught her how to unlock potential in overlooked talent. The Valkyries’ success demonstrates the power of providing resources, responsibility, and trust to players who were once undervalued, proving the organization’s philosophy and Nakase’s leadership were key to their championship run.

title: Premier League managers hold firm as first sacking looms after early season stability
content:

In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change, indicating that the early part of the campaign is often a period of stability.

The 2026‑27 season began with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026, a factor that has likely contributed to the current lack of dismissals.  The clubs have therefore been given a chance to shape their squads as they see fit without the pressure of an early change in leadership.

However, with roughly a quarter of the season already played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.  The looming break could prompt clubs to make a decision if results do not meet expectations.

Speaking during a Fox News interview, Trump remarked, “Well, if that happens, I guess I’ll become Mr. Veto. I’m not going to let them through,” outlining his proposed strategy for handling a Democratic-controlled Congress.
summary: President Trump said he would become "Mr. Veto" if Democrats take control of Congress. He said he would not let them through and would use his veto power.
author: The Hill

title: Stevens defends last‑minute endorsement of Rogers in Michigan Senate race
content: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens of Michigan defended her late endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers in the state’s Senate race, after having previously supported Democrat Abdul El‑Sayed. Speaking to reporters in Detroit alongside Rogers, Stevens said she is “not turning my back on Democrats” and that the decision is a personal, private one. She added that she still loves the party.
summary: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens of Michigan defended her last‑minute endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race, saying she is not turning her back on Democrats. She said the decision was personal and private and that she still loves the party.
author: The Hill

title: El‑Sayed dismisses late endorsement by former rival Stevens for Rogers
content: Michigan Senate Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed brushed off his former rival Haley Stevens’s surprising and late endorsement of GOP nominee Mike Rogers, saying on Sunday it didn’t matter and that he was focused on issues in his state. “At the end of the day, I actually don’t think about Haley Stevens,” El-Sayed told reporters, flanked…
summary: Abdul El‑Sayed brushed off former rival Haley Stevens’s late endorsement of GOP nominee Mike Rogers, saying it did not matter. He said he is focused on state issues and does not think about Stevens.
author: The Hill

title: DNC Chair Ken Martin defends El-Sayed and Peltola amid GOP attacks
content: DNC Chair Ken Martin defended Democratic Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) against recent GOP attacks. These defenses come as the party prepares for potential post-election legal disputes. Martin specifically asserted that statements made by Dr. El-Sayed are true, emphasizing that Michiganders’ primary concerns differ from the current political rhetoric.
summary: DNC Chair Ken Martin defended Democratic Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) against recent GOP attacks. The party is concerned about post-election legal fights.
author: The Hill

title: Schumer calls Stevens’s endorsement of Mike Rogers a despicable betrayal
content: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N. Y.) ripped Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) over her eleventh hour endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers in the competitive Michigan Senate contest. “This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens,” Schumer wrote Sunday on the social platform X, reiterating his support for Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in the race. Schumer’s remarks are…
summary: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer criticized Rep. Haley Stevens for endorsing Republican Mike Rogers late in the Michigan Senate race. Schumer reaffirmed his support for Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in the contest.
author: The Hill

title: Trump praises Democrat Haley Stevens for endorsing GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers
content: President Trump praised Rep. Haley Stevens (D‑Mich.) on Sunday for endorsing GOP Senate candidate former Rep. Mike Rogers (Mich.). He called the endorsement “BIG” and described Stevens as a “Highly Respected Democrat” who narrowly lost the primary to Abdul Mohamed El‑Sayed.
summary: President Trump on Sunday commended Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) for her endorsement of GOP Senate candidate former Rep.

title: RNC urges Michigan to note Haley Stevens' endorsement of Mike Rogers
content: The Republican National Committee (RNC) on Sunday said Michigan “should take notice” of Rep. Haley Stevens’s (D-Mich.) endorsement of her former opponent in the Michigan Senate race Republican Mike Rogers. “When Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who ran against Abdul El-Sayed and knows him better than anyone, stands with Mike Rogers, Michigan should take notice,” RNC spokesperson…
summary: The Republican National Committee said Michigan should take notice of Rep. Haley Stevens’s endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers. Stevens, a Democrat who previously ran against Abdul El‑Sayed in the Senate race, is backing Rogers, the RNC spokesperson said.
author: The Hill

title: RNC Chair Joe Gruters Acknowledges Republican Voter Turnout Problem
content: Republican National Committee (RNC) chair Joe Gruters acknowledged that Republicans are facing issues with voter turnout amid heightened pressure for the GOP to maintain control of Congress. “Is there a turnout problem for Republicans?” NewsNation’s Chris Stirewalt asked Gruters on “The Hill Sunday.” “Yes, but Democrats tend to turn out early. We tend to vote…
summary: Joe Gruters said Republicans have a voter turnout problem amid pressure to keep control of Congress. He noted that Democrats tend to turn out early while Republicans tend to vote later.
author: The Hill

title: Midterms to test nation's political confidence and direction
content: The upcoming midterm elections are expected to test the nation's political confidence and sense of security. This assessment may persist for the days and weeks following the vote, potentially extending further into the future.
summary: The midterms may test the political confidence of parts of the nation in the coming days and weeks. The test could continue for some time to come.
author: NPR Politics

title: Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit to block Alaska Senate results if GOP incumbent loses
content: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit filed by the Trump administration seeking to block the certification of results from Alaska's U.S. Senate race. The legal action, described as highly unusual, aimed to prevent certification if the Republican incumbent lost the election.
summary: A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit by the Trump administration that tried to block certification of Alaska Senate results if the Republican incumbent lost. The lawsuit was described as highly unusual.
author: NPR Politics

title: Democrats Lead in Midterm Polls Amid Political Moment
content: Polls show Democrats with an advantage in the midterm election but there are potential limitations and results may take a while to roll in. (Image credit: Andrew Harnik)

title: Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy Hospitalized After Stroke
content: Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy was hospitalized over the weekend after experiencing numbness in his arm. His chief of staff stated that Murphy is responding well to treatment and is expected to make a full recovery.
summary: Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy was taken to the hospital this weekend after experiencing numbness in his arm. His chief of staff reports he is responding well to treatment and is expected to make a full recovery.
author: NPR Politics

title: Haley Stevens Endorses GOP Candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate Race
content: Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race, spurning Abdul El-Sayed. This decision came after Stevens was scheduled to attend a unity event with El-Sayed, who had defeated her in the Democratic primary.
summary: Rep. Haley Stevens was scheduled to attend a unity event with Abdul El-Sayed, who beat her in the Democratic primary. Instead, she endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.

title: Vision-language AI agent could speed radiologists' ultrasound interpretation
content: Researchers at the University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine are developing a vision-language AI agent to assist radiologists in interpreting ultrasounds. The team aims to streamline radiological workflows, improve efficiency, and help identify patients requiring urgent surgery for faster treatment in emergency settings.
summary: Researchers at the University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine are investigating a vision-language AI agent to help radiologists interpret ultrasounds faster and more accurately. They also aim to streamline radiologists' work, quickly identify patients who may need urgent surgery, and speed up the path to treatment.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Virgin Media O2 to cut thousands of jobs
content: Virgin Media O2 is set to cut thousands of jobs, according to the BBC. The broadband provider has not yet finalized the exact number of roles to be eliminated, though it is expected to impact a sizeable portion of its workforce.
summary: Virgin Media O2 is planning to cut thousands of jobs. The exact number of roles to be axed has not been finalized, but it will likely be a sizeable chunk of its workforce, according to the BBC.
author: BBC Business

title: Conifers in Southern Hemisphere Grow Four Times Faster, More Drought-Resistant
content: A study covering 192 sites across four continents found that conifers planted in the Southern Hemisphere grow up to four times faster and exhibit greater drought resistance than those in their native ranges. These findings highlight how some trees thrive far from home, with implications for the effectiveness of carbon sinks.
summary: Researchers studied 192 sites across four continents and found that conifers planted in the Southern Hemisphere grow up to four times faster than those in their native ranges. The Southern Hemisphere conifers also show greater drought resistance.
author: Phys.org

title: Mediterranean Climate Not Tropical Despite Warmer Seas and Shifting Pressures
content: Nowhere in the Iberian Peninsula or the Balearic Islands has a tropical climate—for this to be the case, the average temperature in the coldest month would have to be 18°C (64 degrees Fahrenheit) or higher. The contrast between Spain's winters and summers, and the low temperatures reached in winter, do not resemble those of any tropical climate.
summary: The Iberian Peninsula and Balearic Islands do not have a tropical climate because the average temperature in the coldest month is below 18°C. The contrast between Spain's winters and summers and the low winter temperatures do not match tropical climate patterns.
author: Phys.org

title: From Italy to Croatia, a warming climate threatens prized white truffles
content: Tino Marolo and his dog Stella search in the dark woods of Piedmont, guided by a flashlight, for one of Italy’s most prized culinary treasures hidden beneath the soil. The hunt underscores a growing concern: a warming climate threatens these prized white truffles from Italy to Croatia.
summary: Guided by the beam of a flashlight, Tino Marolo follows his dog Stella through the darkness of a Piedmont woodland, searching for one of Italy's most prized culinary treasures hidden beneath the soil.
author: Phys.org

title: Singapore Tests Chilled Beams and Passive Displacement to Reduce Energy Use
content: Singapore, long dubbed an “air‑conditioned nation,” is exploring alternatives to its heavy reliance on cooling. The country is experimenting with options such as chilled beams and “passive displacement” to reduce the energy consumption of its air‑conditioning systems.
summary: Singapore, long dubbed an 'air-conditioned nation,' is testing cooling alternatives. The alternatives include chilled beams and 'passive displacement' to curb its thirst for energy-guzzling air conditioning.
author: Phys.org

title: Delhi Implements Higher Parking Fees and Work-From-Home Orders to Tackle Smog
content: Authorities in New Delhi announced new anti‑pollution measures on Sunday, raising parking fees and issuing work‑from‑home orders. The actions aim to curb the toxic smog that plagues the city, which is recognized as one of the world’s most polluted capitals.
summary: Authorities in New Delhi raised parking fees and issued work‑from‑home orders on Sunday. The measures aim to curb toxic smog in the city.
author: Phys.org

title: Perseverance uses spacesuit swatches to test if Martian dust is less abrasive than lunar dust
content: NASA’s Perseverance rover carries tiny swatches of spacesuit material—each less than a square inch (6.5 cm²)—among its sensors, cameras and navigation tools. The swatches are used to evaluate the potential damage caused by Martian dust. According to the title, these samples suggest that Mars dust may be less abrasive than lunar dust.
summary: NASA's Mars rover Perseverance is wearing small swatches of spacesuit material. The swatches, each less than a square inch in size, are helping scientists assess whether Martian dust is less abrasive than lunar dust.
author: Phys.org

title: Fiona Walker's report reveals Covid deaths 4-6x higher for UK learning disability patients
content: The Covid pandemic shed an unforgiving light on health and social care inequalities. The lessons have yet to be absorbed The fear that so many felt as the death toll rose during the Covid pandemic was magnified for Fiona Walker. “I know from experience they wouldn’t have valued my life,” she says, in a new report on the treatment of people with learning disabilities during the crisis. The 1.5 million people in the UK with learning disabilities, and their families, had reason for concern. Death rates in England were four to six times higher than average for people with learning disabilities. As is now well established, the pandemic did not create inequalities; it exposed and intensified them. People with learning disabilities die on average 19.5 years earlier than people without, and deaths are almost twice as likely to be classed as avoidable.
summary: The Covid pandemic shed an unforgiving light on health and social care inequalities. The lessons have yet to be absorbed The fear that so many felt as the death toll rose during the Covid pandemic was magnified for Fiona Walker.
author: Guardian Science

title: Show HN: HackerBooks aggregates 16.5k books mentioned on Hacker News
content:
A developer has launched HackerBooks, a website designed to track books mentioned on Hacker News, inspired by Karpathy’s HackerTube. The site catalogues approximately 16,500 books that at least two distinct HN commenters have referenced between 2007 and the present. Each entry links back to the specific comments where the book was mentioned, and the underlying data is available for download from the site’s about page.

The creator states that Claude Opus 5.5 wrote almost all of the project, including the data pipeline and the website itself, while the developer handled steering, decision-making, and purchasing the domain. The tool counts all mentions, meaning both praise and criticism contribute to a book’s tally. The project has garnered 511 points and 130 comments on Hacker News, with the creator inviting users to report missing titles or incorrect matches.
summary: HackerBooks, created with Claude’s assistance, lists about 16.5 k books that at least two Hacker News commenters have mentioned since 2007, with each book linking back to the comments. The author steered the project, purchased the domain, and provides downloadable data from the site’s about page.
author: Hacker News

title: Ask HN: Users seek privacy‑focused TVs for Apple TV use, 60‑80″ 4K display
content:
A user on Hacker News posted a question seeking a privacy‑focused television. The poster has not owned a TV for years and wants a 60‑to‑80‑inch 4K display with a minimum 60 Hz refresh rate. They are willing to pay a premium and have heard that Apple TV offers better privacy than many native smart‑TV apps. The user asks whether certain TVs pair better with Apple TV for privacy and wants to know what success others have had.

The post includes a link to the discussion thread on Hacker News (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50328896). The thread has 17 points and 19 comments, indicating some community engagement around the topic.
summary: A Hacker News user asked for recommendations for a privacy‑respecting TV sized 60‑80 inches with 4K resolution and at least 60 Hz, willing to pay a premium. The user prefers using Apple TV as the sole smart platform and asked which TVs pair best for privacy, receiving 17 points and 19 comments.
author: Hacker News

title: Dying star 1,600 ly away shows two dust rings from former planets
content:
Astronomers have identified a dying star 1,600 light‑years from Earth that is surrounded by two rings of gas and dust.  

The rings are thought to be remnants of planetary bodies that the star once hosted.
summary: A dying star 1,600 light-years from Earth is surrounded by two rings of gas and dust. Astronomers believe the rings are remnants of the planetary bodies the star once hosted.
author: Wired

title: Playable version of canceled Portal prequel F‑Stop leaked
content:
Leakers have assembled a playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F‑Stop. Most of the assets for the build came from the massive 12‑terabyte leak that dropped in August; the leak did not include the game’s source code or map data.  

Those missing pieces apparently surfaced on the Valve Cut Content Discord this week, allowing a nearly complete version to be pieced together.  

Some dialog and elements from F‑Stop eventually found their way into Portal 2. The prequel differs from the mainline Portal games by centering on a camera mechanic that lets players capture an item by taking its picture and then place it elsewhere using the resulting Polaroid.
summary: Leakers have pieced together a playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F-Stop. Most of the assets came from the massive 12-terabyte leak that dropped this August.
author: The Verge

title: Apple’s HomeView may gain security camera mode with HomeKit Secure Video
content:
Reddit user pdfu has uncovered clues in the HomeView 27.2 firmware that suggest Apple may be adding security‑camera functionality to its smart‑home hub. The firmware strings reference a “security camera mode” that includes motion detection, live streaming, and recording options, along with privacy features.

A setup page in the code explicitly states: “Your HomeView can be used as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video.” According to pdfu, the camera feeds would be viewable only by members of the home and would display an indicator light and emit a sound when the feed is being watched or when recording begins. The analysis stops short of detailing further privacy measures.
summary: Reddit user pdfu found hints hidden in the HomeView 27.2 code that Apple could be adding security camera features to its smart home hub. The strings describe a security camera mode with motion detection, live streaming, and recording options, as well as privacy functions.
author: The Verge

title: Police Chief Eric Fadden disconnects Flock cameras after council fails to respond
content:
More municipalities are ending contracts with surveillance firm Flock Safety, but several are encountering obstacles. In Plymouth, Minnesota, the city council voted in September to terminate its agreement with Flock, yet the company did not respond to the city’s cancellation request. The cameras stayed operational for more than a month without acknowledgment from Flock.

Consequently, Police Chief Eric Fadden ordered staff to unplug the devices. He said that after receiving no reply for over a week, he directed the power cords be disconnected to ensure the cameras were no longer functioning.
summary: Police Chief Eric Fadden disconnects Flock cameras after council fails to respond.
author: The Verge

title: Charisma as a Red Flag: How a Bar Conversation Revealed Manipulation
content: Today’s crop of smooth talkers tap directly into a specific evolutionary vulnerability. Here’s how to defend yourself Recently, I was alone in a bar waiting for a friend. To pass the time, I started chatting to a stranger. He had an easy, confident way of speaking, which I admired. We discussed topics I know little about: the instability of modern economies, the feasibility of commercial space travel, the likelihood of a coup in Russia. I found myself leaning in and asking questions: I felt as if I could learn a lot from this person. We eventually got to psychology, which is more my wheelhouse. I brooded about how easy it’s become for people to accept strange ideas. “Some people will believe anything,” he observed. “Some people even believe the Earth is round!” It’s increasingly difficult to ignore how fragmented and bizarre our beliefs have become. We live in our own echo chambers, defined by the channels, feeds and influencers we follow. As a result we can arrive at very polarised conclusions about vaccines, the climate, gender, geopolitics, the shape of the Earth and everything else. Disagreements on topics like these frequently damage relationships, alienate friends and estrange loved ones.
summary: The narrator recounts a conversation with a charismatic stranger in a bar who discussed topics the narrator knew little about, including economics, space travel, and geopolitics. The narrator reflects that charisma can lead people to accept bizarre ideas, contributing to polarized beliefs that damage relationships.
author: Guardian Technology

title: 2026 Youth Olympic Games open in Dakar, first Olympic event in Africa
content: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games have officially kicked off in Senegal. Crowds gathered for Saturday's opening ceremony, featuring hundreds of drummers and dancers celebrating Senegalese and wider African culture, in keeping with the Games' motto: “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates”. It is the first-ever Olympic sporting event to be held on the African continent, but comes as Senegal faces an economic crisis. The country's president has said he wants to turn sport into an “economic and social engine”. The Games also come amid a government crackdown on LGBTQ+ people. Nearly 3,000 teenagers from more than 200 countries are competing in around a dozen sports, including athletics, beach wrestling and a five-a-side version of baseball. Jean-Loup Chappelet, Professor at Lausanne University and Olympics specialist, shares further insights.
summary: 2026 Youth Olympic Games open in Dakar, first Olympic event in Africa.
author: France 24

title: Senegal hosts first Youth Olympic Games in Africa
content:
Senegal hosts the first Olympic event on the African continent. The Youth Olympics marked the first African Games in over 130 years, opening ceremony led by Senegal’s president in Dakar.  

A total of 136 Senegalese athletes are competing, with the event supported by 6,000 local volunteers.
summary: The Youth Olympic Games opened in Dakar, marking the first Olympic event held on the African continent in over 130 years and were inaugurated by Senegal’s president. The games feature 136 Senegalese athletes and are supported by 6,000 local volunteers.
author: France 24

title: Kherson ceasefire ends Sunday after Russia declines extension
content: The longest truce of the war in Ukraine, confined to the Kherson region, was scheduled to end on Sunday evening after Russia declined to extend it. The pause, which began on Tuesday, had allowed a humanitarian mission to the Russian‑occupied town of Olechky.
summary: The longest truce of the war in Ukraine, localized in Kherson, was set to end on Sunday evening after Russia refused to extend it. The pause, which began on Tuesday, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian‑occupied town of Olechky.
author: France 24

title: France sees third weekend of protests over living costs, education, largely peaceful
content: France experienced its third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, drawing more than 320,000 participants. While most demonstrations remained peaceful, police deployed tear gas to disperse clashes, and authorities recorded over 770 arrests nationwide. France24 journalist Jamie Smith‑Maillet provided additional commentary.
summary: More than 320,000 people protested across France for the third consecutive weekend over living costs and education, and most demonstrations remained peaceful. Police used tear gas in some clashes and authorities reported more than 770 arrests nationwide.
author: France 24

title: Evacuations from Oleshky end during first humanitarian truce
content:
Residents of Oleshky who had asked to leave were reunited with their families in Ukraine on Saturday, October 31, concluding the evacuations carried out during the first humanitarian truce of the war.  

The city, situated on the front line and under Russian occupation, remains in a humanitarian crisis, with civilians lacking even basic necessities. A localized ceasefire has been in place since Tuesday, as reported by France 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze.
summary: Residents of Oleshky who had requested evacuation were reunited with their loved ones in Ukraine on Saturday, October 31. The front‑line city under Russian occupation, facing a humanitarian crisis, has been under a localised ceasefire since Tuesday, the first humanitarian truce of the war.
author: France 24

title: Indian opposition protests in New Delhi against Modi government and voter list review
content: Thousands joined an opposition protest in New Delhi on Sunday, where India’s opposition parties demonstrated against Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and a nationwide voter‑list review that has sparked demonstrations since the summer. The rally was led by the youth movement Cockroach Janta Party, according to reporter Eliza Herbert.
summary: India's opposition parties staged major protests in New Delhi on Sunday against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and a nationwide voter list review. The demonstrations were led by the youth movement Cockroach Janta Party, Eliza Herbert reports.
author: France 24

title: 115 sailors launch Route du Rhum from Saint‑Malo in mild weather
content:
The solo transatlantic Route du Rhum race launched from Saint‑Malo on Sunday with 115 sailors setting off in mild weather. The fleet left at 12:02 GMT, heading along the Brittany coast in light winds toward a mandatory checkpoint near Cap Fréhel, where spectators had gathered.

Competitor Nicolas d’Estais called the conditions “ideal” before boarding his yacht Café Joyeux. The departure was reported from Saint‑Malo by Selina Sykes.
summary: The 115 sailors competing in the solo transatlantic Route du Rhum set sail from Saint‑Malo on Sunday at 12:02 GMT in mild conditions. Boats headed along the Brittany coast toward a checkpoint near Cap Fréhel, where crowds gathered, and competitor Nicolas d’Estais said the conditions were ideal before boarding his yacht Café Joyeux.
author: France 24

title: Gavin Lee reviews Michigan “betrayal” and midterm maneuvers on France 24 Spotlight
content: France 24’s Spotlight Presenter Gavin Lee assesses the last minute campaign dramas and takes an US election overview on the ‘must watch states’ alongside Professor Donald Green, Professor of Political Science at Columbia University and co-author of the definitive book ‘Get Out the Vote’, and foreign affairs analyst Laurie Dundon, who previously served in the U.
